title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic non 3
abstract: We classify the minimal faithful Alt(6)-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful Alt(n)- and Sym(n)-modules with an additive dimension

title: Finite Symplectic Automorphisms of Hyperkähler Manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-Type Act Trivially on Discriminant Groups
abstract: We give an alternative proof of Mongardi's result that every finite group of symplectic automorphisms of a hyperkähler manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type acts trivially on the discriminant groups of its second cohomology lattice and its coinvariant lattice. The proof combines sphere-packing bounds, Vinberg's reflection chambers and structure results on even $2$-elementary lattices.

title: On families of copulas and quasi-copulas homeomorphic to the Hilbert cube and related results
abstract: Working with tools from infinite-dimensional topology and using measure-theoretic ideas we analyze numerous well-known fami\-lies of copu\-las and quasi-copulas from a topological perspective, prove that most of them are homeomorphic to the Hilbert cube $\mathcal{H}$ and hence have the Fixed Point as well as the Disjoint Cells property. Working with so-called $Z$-sets, we then study how large one set is within another. Doing so, in order to show that a set $A$ is small/topologically negligible within a compact metric space $(Ω,m)$, we construct a homeomorphism $h: [0,1] \times \mathcal{H} \to Ω$ mapping $\{0\} \times \mathcal{H}$ to $A$. The obtained results are to a certain extent surprising since various supposedly small families are topologically large.

title: Character cyclic amenability of Banach algebras
abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the notion of character cyclic amenability for Banach algebras, which combines the cyclicity condition on derivations with the character-dependent module structure arising in character amenability. We establish several basic properties of this notion and investigate its behavior under standard Banach algebra constructions. In particular, we study character cyclic amenability for opposite algebras, projective tensor products, l1-direct sums, quotient algebras, dense homomorphic images, and theta-Lau products. We also provide examples illustrating the relationship between character cyclic amenability and other amenability-type properties, including examples showing that character cyclic amenability does not imply cyclic amenability. Finally, we characterize character cyclic amenability for module extension Banach algebras in terms of phi-cyclic derivations and derivations associated with the underlying Banach module.

title: K3 surfaces with finite automorphism group in positive characteristic
abstract: We classify K3 surfaces with finite automorphism group in positive characteristic. The classification is the same as over the complex numbers, except when the base field is $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$.

title: Trace-minimal graphs maximizing the number of spanning trees
abstract:
A classical problem in spectral graph theory is to determine, among all simple graphs with a fixed number of vertices and edges, those that maximize the number of spanning trees. Such graphs are called $t$-optimal. Petingi and Rodríguez [Discr. Math. 244 (2002), 351-373] reduced the construction of infinitely many $t$-optimal graphs to the determination of almost-regular graphs with a minimum number of induced $3$-paths, known as almost-regular $ν$-min graphs. They conjectured that the class of $d$-regular $ν$-min graphs is invariant under the addition or deletion of copies of the complete graph $K_{d+1}$, which would provide a method to construct large families of $t$-optimal graphs. This conjecture was recently verified for $d\in \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ by Gong et al. [Discr. Math. 349(4), 2026].
  In this work, we establish an asymptotic version of this conjecture. We prove that the class of $d$-regular $ν$-min graphs on at least $n$ vertices is invariant under the addition or deletion of copies of $K_{d+1}$ whenever $d\geq 3$ and $n\geq d^3$. In addition, we introduce a new method to construct $t$-optimal graphs based on the concept of trace-minimal graphs, originally introduced by Ábrego et al. [Linear Algebra Appl. 412 (2006), 161-221]. As a consequence, we obtain infinitely many graphs that are both trace-minimal and $t$-optimal.

title: Non-local to local limit for stochastic conservation laws
abstract: This work proves the convergence of stochastic nonlocal conservation laws, with spatially inhomogeneous noise, to stochastic conservation laws when the range of particle interaction vanishes. This provides rigorous justification for a class of stochastic conservation laws that has received considerable attention in the last decade. To handle technical challenges such as gradient-dependent noise, modified versions of the equations with specific cutoff boundaries are utilized and new uniform estimates to ensure stability during the limiting process are established. In addition, the work demonstrates that this convergence depends on the presence of a viscous term, as a counterexample shows that without it, the limiting solution may fail to be an entropy solution.

title: Quadratic Reciprocity via Vandermonde Matrix
abstract: This paper presents a proof of the law of quadratic reciprocity using the Vandermonde matrix and Zolotarev's lemma.

title: Structured Time-Frequency Representation for Channel Prediction
abstract: Accurate CSI forecasting is essential for mitigating channel aging and supporting reliable downlink transmission in high-mobility wireless systems. In FDD systems, forecasting future DL CSI from historical UL observations requires joint temporal extrapolation and cross-band inference. However, defining historical UL as the input and future DL as the target does not specify how elapsed time and UL-to-DL band separation should be represented in a pretrained predictor's positional space. FAR-CSI establishes an FDD-aware representation of channel forecasting within a joint temporal and operating-band positional field. Within this field, historical UL observations and future DL targets occupy segregated regions according to their temporal and operating-band roles, preserving the distinction between observed UL context and unobserved DL prediction targets. This representation is instantiated through a unified structured routing rule that governs encoder positional assignment, decoder-field reconstruction, and future-DL target selection, ensuring the same FDD geometry is preserved from contextual encoding to prediction readout. Under matched backbone, initialization, and training conditions, FDD-aware routing reduces NMSE by 21.44\% relative to generic routing. Across the evaluated FDD baselines, FAR-CSI achieves higher CSI prediction accuracy and MRT-based spectral efficiency, while retaining its predictive advantage across mobility conditions, prediction horizons, reduced training-data regimes, and noisy historical observations.

title: Monte Carlo Power Iteration Algorithms: Convergence, Analysis and Application to Reactor Criticality Calculations
abstract: We study Monte Carlo power iteration algorithms in the context of reactor criticality simulations. Under mild conditions on the underlying physical system and the algorithmic structure, we derive explicit error bounds, which are to the best of our knowledge the first rigorous results for such methods which are ubiquitous in nuclear engineering. This is done by exploiting connections to Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms, and extending recent developments about stochastic neutron transport. We demonstrate the applicability of our results by considering a concrete version of the Monte Carlo power iteration algorithm as well as variance reduction schemes.

title: The Keller problem for the lowest positive eigenvalue of Dirac operators with Lorentz scalar potentials
abstract: We study the Keller problem for the Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_m - Vβ$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and minimize its lowest positive eigenvalue over all potentials $V$ with prescribed $L^p$ norm. We prove that optimal potentials always exist and that the corresponding eigenspinors solve the nonlinear Soler equation. This provides a variational proof of existence of solitary waves for this equation. We prove that there are no zero modes for such operators in dimensions $1$ and $2$, and conjecture that zero mode may exist in dimension $3$. In dimension $d = 2$, we provide numerical evidence that the optimal potentials concentrate on flower-shape regions, which are not necessarily radial, showing that Faber--Krahn type results may fail for such Dirac operators. In dimension $1$, all quantities are explicit.

title: The reverse isoperimetric inequality for convex shapes included in a triangle
abstract: We establish a sharp reverse isoperimetric inequality for convex subsets of a triangle under a prescribed area constraint. Given a triangle $T$ and an area fraction $η\in(0,1)$, we determine the set with maximal perimeter among convex bodies $K\subset T$ satisfying $|K|=η|T|$ and characterize the equality cases. Every maximizer is a triangle, and the optimal configuration is obtained by retaining a longest side of $T$ and placing the third vertex on a shortest side, at the position determined by the area constraint. This characterization yields an explicit expression for the maximal perimeter in terms of $η$ and the side lengths of $T$.

title: Finite-Branch Multipliers on a Hölder Algebra: Commutants, Norm Closures, and Essential Spectra
abstract: Noninjective multiplication symbols allow commuting operators to mix function values along their fibers, while Hölder regularity constrains this mixing at branch points. We study these operators on the Banach algebra $A_β$, $0<β<1$, defined by a restricted interval-variation condition. For $u(t)=t(1-t)$, we determine the full commutant $\{M_u\}'=\mathscr C_β$, including operators whose reflection coefficients need not belong to $A_β$. Separately, we characterize the operator-norm closure $J_β$ of the regular multiplication--reflection subalgebra of $\mathscr C_β$, obtain two-sided norm-distance estimates, and find a complemented copy of $\ell^\infty/c_0$ in the Banach-space quotient $\mathscr C_β/J_β$. Every $T\in\mathscr C_β$ satisfies $σ(T)=σ_{\mathrm{ap}}(T)=σ_{\mathrm{usf}}(T)=σ_{\mathrm{ess}}(T)$, and Fredholmness is equivalent to invertibility. For multipliers with finitely many full bi-Lipschitz branches, we also characterize their full commutants and establish the same spectral equalities for every commuting operator. For the regular finite-branch algebra, we establish an exact norm-closure criterion using weighted local Hölder defects and separate row-difference conditions, even when several folds share a level.

title: Recognizing convergence actions as proper isometric actions on hyperbolic spaces
abstract: Relying merely on B.I. (a.k.a. Bowditch's intelligence), we show that whenever a group $G$ admits a convergence action on a compact perfect metrizable space $M$, there is a hyperbolic space $X$ along with a proper isometric action of $G$ on $X$ inducing a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $f:M \rightarrow \partial X.$ This answers a question by Misha Kapovich.

title: A new infinite family of covers of complete graphs that admit a half-transitive action of a Suzuki simple group
abstract: We construct a new infinite family of antipodal $2(q-1)$-covers of complete graphs $K_{q^2+1}$ of diameter $3$, where $q=2^{2e+1}\ge 8$, admitting a half-transitive action of the Suzuki simple group $Sz(q)$. We further show that each constructed cover admits an involutory automorphism interchanging the two $Sz(q)$-orbits on arcs, which yields that its full automorphism group is arc-transitive.

title: $L^p$ Convergence of AMV Laplacians on completions of Riemannian manifolds
abstract: We study conditions for the $L^p$ convergence of the AMV Laplacian $Δ_r$ on completions of Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$. The condition invloves the Minkowski dimension of the set $\overline{M} \setminus M$ and how much the curvature is blowing up around $S$. We build a concrete family of sets that satisfies these conditions, and provide an example of non convergence when these conditions are not met.

title: Existence of uniformly most reliable two-terminal graphs with distance constraints
abstract: A two-terminal graph is a simple graph equipped with two distinguished vertices, called terminals. Let $T_{n,m}$ be the class consisting of all non-isomorphic two-terminal graphs on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. Let $G$ be any two-terminal graph in $T_{n,m}$, and let $d$ be any positive integer. For every $ρ\in [0,1]$, the \emph{$d$-constrained two-terminal reliability of $G$ at $ρ$}, denoted $R_G^d(ρ)$, is the probability that $G$ has some path of length at most $d$ joining its terminals after each of its edges is independently deleted with probability $ρ$. We say $G$ is a \emph{$d$-uniformly most reliable two-terminal graph} ($d$-UMRTTG) if for each $H$ in $T_{n,m}$ and every $ρ\in [0,1]$ it holds that $R_{G}^d(ρ)\geq R_{H}^{d}(ρ)$. Previous works studied the existence of $d$-UMRTTG in $T_{n,m}$ when $d$ is greater than or equal to $n-1$, or equivalently, when the distance constraint is dropped. In this work, a characterization of all $1$-UMRTTGs and $2$-UMRTTGs is given. Several structural properties of 3-UMRTTGs are established. For every $d\geq 3$, we prove the existence of a unique $d$-UMRTTG in $T_{n,\binom{n}{2}-1}$. In contrast, for every $d\geq 4$ and every $n\geq 11$, no $d$-UMRTTG exists in $T_{n,m}$ whenever $20\leq m\leq 3n-9$ or $3n-5\leq m\leq \binom{n}{2}-2$. Additionally, for each $d\geq 5$, it is proved that no $d$-UMRTTG exists in $T_{n,m}$ when $n\geq 11$ and $m=3n-8$.

title: Uniqueness and large-time continuous dependence in a doubly degenerate nutrient taxis system
abstract:
\[
  u_t = \nabla \cdot (uv\nabla u) - χ\nabla\cdot (u^2 v\nabla v) + \ell uv,
  \qquad \qquad
  v_t = Δv - uv, \] is considered in a smoothly bounded domain $Ω\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ and with $χ\ge 0$ and $\ell\ge 0$.
  Within a suitable concept of solvability, a statement on uniqueness of solutions emanating from initial data $(u_0,v_0)$ is derived under the mere assumption that $u_0\in L^\infty(Ω)$ and $v_0\in W^{1,\infty}(Ω)$ are such that $u_0\ge 0$ and $v_0>0$ in $\overlineΩ$; in particular, no condition on continuity of $u_0$ is imposed.
  This result is thereafter used to reveal that in physcally meaningful scenarios, for any initial data which are additionally assumed to be continuous and nontrivial, such solutions can always be found, and that these solutions depend continuously on the initial distributions not only in bounded sets of the form $Ω\times (0,T)$, but actually throughout $Ω\times (0,\infty)$, in a suitable sense.

title: Setting Things Straight: On the Straightness and Non-Straightness of Two-Step Rectified Flow
abstract: Rectified flow (RF) is an ODE-based generative modeling framework that has achieved remarkable success in practice over the past few years. By design, RF seeks to produce flows that have a high degree of straightness, in the sense that the resulting ODE trajectories can be obtained with relatively few (ideally, one) sampling steps. However, a rigorous analysis of straightness or near-straightness of RF flows remains missing in the literature. In this paper, we study settings in which the coupling generated by two-step RF is provably straight at the population level. We provide a complete characterization in two popular classes of data distributions: (i) smooth, strongly log-concave densities and (ii) Gaussian mixture models. Our main results yield sharp conditions for the coupling generated by two-step RF to be straight. Non-straight couplings are constructed when these conditions fail, which demonstrate the sharpness of these conditions. Using the theory developed on the straightness of two-step RF, we propose a notion of approximate straightness that measures the straightness of the learned couplings and can be estimated from the data. We describe a procedure for constructing asymptotic confidence intervals for our proposed notion of approximate straightness and propose a data-driven method for selecting the number of reflow rounds in multiple iterations of RF.

title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
abstract: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

title: Using the Blackwell-Cover Guessing Strategy to Separate Unobserved Bernoulli Trials - II
abstract: In a prior paper, we investigated what could be said about the number in the pair that was not observed when we employed the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy. In this paper, we generalize prior results to arbitrary distributions. We use a variant of the BlackwellCover strategy ro take pairs of coins chosen from a mixture of two different distributions G and H such that one of the coins is flipped, and as a result of that flip the unobserved (unflipped) coin is placed in one of two sets A and B. We show that, regardless of which distributions are used for G and H, there are situations in which this can be done so that the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in A is less than the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in B. What makes this result surprising, in addition to its generality, is a comparison with a corresponding result for marbles. If one knows that one will always be weighing one of two marbles with different specific weights, such as 10g and 20g, knowing the weight of the marble being weighed automatically determines the weight of the other. However, even if one knows that one will be flipping one of two coins with specific heads probabilities such as 1/3 and 2/3, the outcome of the flip of one of the coins will not immediately enable one to conclude anything about the heads probability of the unflipped coin, which is where the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy comes into play.

title: On Hamilton cycles in quasiprimitive graphs of order $2pq$
abstract: Let $p>q>5$ be primes. We determine the socles and corresponding actions of quasiprimitive imprimitive groups of degree $2pq$, all of which are almost simple. Using this classification, we prove that a connected graph of order $2pq$ admitting a quasiprimitive automorphism group contains a Hamilton cycle, except possibly for three specified families of actions with socle $\PSL(2,p)$ or $\PSL(2,q^2)$.

title: Retriangular numbers and affine maps between polygonal numbers
abstract: A positive integer $a$ is called \emph{retriangular} if there is a positive integer $b$ such that $aT+b$ is a triangular number whenever $T$ is. We show that the retriangular numbers are exactly the odd squares greater than $1$, and that for each of them $b$ is unique. The proof rests on a rigidity principle: a non-constant affine map carrying the values of one quadratic sequence into the values of another is induced by an affine map of the plane sending the vertex of one parabola to the vertex of the other. We use it to classify all affine maps between sets of polygonal numbers; the $s$-gonal numbers map affinely into the $t$-gonal numbers if and only if $M_t\mid M_s$, where $M_s=2(s-2)/\gcd(s,4)$ defines a bijection from $\{3,4,5,\dots\}$ onto the positive integers. We also treat sparse data, polynomial maps, figurate numbers of higher degree and sums of two triangular numbers, and we study the monoid of affine self-maps of an arbitrary set of integers. For the $s$-gonal numbers this monoid is an arithmetical congruence monoid, and the factorization of self-maps into irreducible ones is unique only for triangular and square numbers.

title: Filling knots and essential geodesic systole
abstract: We prove that every closed, orientable $3$--manifold contains hyperbolic knots with arbitrarily large essential geodesic systole. That is, for any $3$--manifold $M$, and $R> 0$ there is a hyperbolic knot $K \subset M$ such that every closed geodesic in the knot complement which is non-null-homotopic in $M$ has length at least $R$. The construction also produces filling knots, in the sense of Freedman-Krushkal [FreeKrus2023]. This answers two questions of Biringer.

title: Rank two cohomology jump loci on projective varieties
abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth connected complex projective variety. We give a structure theorem for irreducible components of the reduced rank-two cohomology jump loci on $X$. More precisely, for such a component $Z$, if the general point of $Z$ is projectively virtually abelian or projectively rigid, then either $Z$ is a symmetric square of an algebraic torus, or a quotient of a torus by an involution, or its normalization $Z^ν$ is a torus. If the general point is neither, then either $Z^ν$ is a torus, or an étale quotient of $Q^ν \times T$ where $Q$ is a fixed-determinant, fixed-inertia component of the character variety of some DM-curve.

title: On the diameter and distribution of Sidon sets
abstract:
A Sidon set is a set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers with the property that if $0\neq a-b=c-d$ and $a,b,c,d\in\mathcal{A}$, then $(a,b)=(c,d)$. Our main result is an improved and explicit bound on the diameter of a Sidon set: if $\mathcal{A}$ is a Sidon set with $k\ge 1$ elements, then
  \[\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge k^2 \left(\frac{1}{1 + 0.945/\sqrt{k}}-\frac{0.945}{\sqrt k}\right) -1;\] in particular, $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A})\ge k^2-1.89 k^{3/2}$. This implies that if $\mathcal{A}\subseteq[1,N]$ is a Sidon set, then $|\mathcal{A}| \le N^{1/2}+0.945 \, N^{1/4}+0.447$. Our technique also gives an improved bound for the case of large $k$, namely $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge k^2-1.88607 k^{3/2}$ for $k\ge 483$. A $γ$-Golomb ruler is a set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers with the property that there are not $γ+1$ distinct pairs $(a_i,b_i)\in\mathcal{A}^2$ with $0\neq a_1-b_1=\cdots=a_{γ+1}-b_{γ+1}$. Our diameter bounds extend in a natural way to the case of Golomb rulers. Our techniques can also be adapted to address a number of questions on the distribution of Golomb rulers: we provide upper bounds on the two quantities $\left|a_\ell-a_1 -\frac{\ell-1}{k-1}(a_k-a_1)\right|$ and $\max_{1\le i<k} (a_{i+1}-a_i)$, where $\mathcal{A}=\{a_1<\dots<a_k\}$ is a $γ$-Golomb ruler with $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A})\le (k^2-bk^{3/2})/γ$ (where $b\in \mathbb{R}$ is a free parameter).

title: When Polynomial Multiplication Counts Geometry: Schubert Polynomials and Monk's Rule
abstract: We give a geometric introduction to Schubert polynomial multiplication through point-line flags in the complex projective plane. Moving a prescribed point onto a prescribed line gives a family with local equation $au=λ$, whose limiting curve has two components. The incidence equations and their local multiplicities give a two-term divisor product, using the standard intersection product on classes of algebraic cycles. Permutation labels and Schubert polynomials express the same decomposition as an instance of Monk's rule. For three incidence conditions, each allowing either a point on a prescribed line or a line through a prescribed point, the product has degree six. Under explicit general-position assumptions, direct construction and local equations give six distinct solutions of multiplicity one.

title: Combinatorial description of the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality
abstract: We prove an explicit correspondence between the irreducible finite dimensional representations of the mirabolic quantum group $MU(n)$ and those of the mirabolic Hecke algebra $MH_d$ given by the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality. In particular, this resolves a generalization of a conjecture by the second author. The proof is via a careful analysis of the $MU(n)$-weight spaces and the eigenvalues of the Jucys Murphy elements of $MH_d$ on the mirabolic tensor space.

title: Formal Neighborhood Equivariant Cohomology and Kirwan Surjectivity at Singular Values
abstract:
Let \(G\) be a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly on a symplectic manifold \(M\) with moment map \(μ:M\to\g^*\). For a singular value \(a\) of \(μ\), the symplectic quotient \(μ^{-1}(a)/G\) is stratified and the classical Kirwan map is not defined. We introduce a \emph{formal neighborhood equivariant cohomology} \(\cH_G^*(a)\) using the slice-groupoid Cartan sheaf and the closed embedding \(μ^{-1}(a)/G\hookrightarrow μ^{-1}(U_a)/G\) for a \(G\)-invariant neighborhood \(U_a\) of \(a\). We define a formal Kirwan map
  \[
  κ_{\mathrm{formal}}:H_G^*(M)\longrightarrow \cH_G^*(a).
  \]
  We prove that \(κ_{\mathrm{formal}}\) is surjective under a local \emph{equivariant homotopy retraction} condition on the slice level sets
  \[
  C_x=μ_x^{-1}(a|_{\g_x})\subset S_x,
  \]
  which is satisfied, for example, when \(a\) is a regular value of every slice moment map, or when \(a=0\) and \(C_x\) is a \(G_x\)-equivariant cone. The weakest condition we identify is the existence, for each \(x\inμ^{-1}(a)\), of a local quasi-isomorphism
  \[
  \Car(S_x,G_x)\simeq \cC^\bullet_{C_x}
  \]
  in a \(G_x\)-equivariant neighborhood of the orbit, without requiring a global tubular neighborhood. As an application we recover, in the formal framework, the even-degree surjectivity theorem of Delarue--Ramacher--Schmitt for \(S^1\)-actions and clarify why odd-degree surjectivity fails in general.

title: Deterministic Causal Quantization with Representative States and Bounded Error
abstract:
We study deterministic causal quantization with pathwise error at most $\varepsilon$, using $ω$ shared representatives updated from transmitted addresses alone. For a midpoint realization with first-in, first-out replacement, we compare address entropy rates with process $\varepsilon$-entropy, the least entropy rate of any block quantizer meeting the same constraint. From $\varepsilon$-separated initialization, the gap is at most two bits per sample for every stationary source with finite scalar $\varepsilon$-entropy, without density, independence or mixing assumptions. A causal address-tree argument extends this comparison to any synchronized quantizer with cell overlap $m$, giving $\log_2 m$ bits. Lattice initialization with consistent boundary ownership realizes uniform grids with sharp one-bit scalar and process comparisons. Under an entropy condition and finite Fisher information rate $J$, the gap is at most $2J\varepsilon^2/(π^2\ln 2)$; general initializations add a term of order $ω\varepsilon\sqrt{J}$. The scalar grid estimate gives a nonasymptotic form of Rényi's theorem. Since a grid is causal, the price of causality is at most $\min\{1,2J\varepsilon^2/(π^2\ln 2)\}$ bits per sample, versus the high-resolution squared-error loss $\tfrac12\log_2(πe/6)$. These bounds certify $\varepsilon$-entropy brackets for autoregressive Laplace and Gaussian sources. For memoryless sources, the optimal causal rate equals the scalar $\varepsilon$-entropy.
  For a stationary process on finitely many $2\varepsilon$-separated centers, adding independent uniform noise of width $2\varepsilon$ gives exact Shannon lower-bound equality at every block length, attained by storing those centers. This includes histograms with finitely many bins. Storing two non-lattice centers beats every uniform grid of the same cell width by half a bit per sample.

title: On Open Borel Orbits in Conormal Bundles to Schubert Cells
abstract: Let $C(v)$ denote a Schubert cell in the flag variety $\operatorname{GL}_n/B$, and let $X(w)$ be a Schubert variety containing $C(v)$. Mellit has conjectured that, if $X(w)$ is smooth, the existence of an open $B$-orbit in the conormal bundle to $C(v)$ in $X(w)$ is equivalent to $C(w_0w)$ being contained in the smooth locus of $X(w_0v)$. We prove a stronger version of this conjecture, requiring only that $X(w)$ is factorial. We prove our result by constructing a sequence of graphs associated to the pair $v,w$ such that the existence of a cycle in one of these graphs is equivalent to the non-existence of such an open orbit.

title: On Baireness of the Wijsman Topology
abstract:
We give negative answers to Questions 4.4 and 4.5 in Cao's survey on the Wijsman topology. We construct a metrizable space $Y$ and a compatible metric $d$ such that every finite power $Y^n$ is Baire, while $(\mathrm{CL}(Y),τ_W(d))$ is not Baire. The construction realizes the Vietoris hyperspace of a suitable metric space as an open subspace of a ball hyperspace.
  We also study the set $S_d$ of points having an open $σ$-$d$-totally bounded neighborhood. We prove that Baireness of $(\mathrm{CL}(X),τ_W(d))$ implies Baireness of $S_d$, and that, whenever $S_d$ is dense in $X$, the following three conditions are equivalent: $(\mathrm{CL}(X),τ_W(d))$ is Baire, $X$ is Baire, and $S_d$ is Baire.
  As consequences, we obtain complete characterizations for locally $σ$-$d$-totally bounded metric spaces, countable metric spaces, and $σ$-compact metrizable spaces. In our counterexample, $S_e$ coincides with a non-dense discrete component for every compatible metric $e$, showing that the density assumption is essential.

title: Smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and del Pezzo cone points
abstract: We give a necessary and sufficient homological criterion for smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees five, six and seven, or over a smooth quadric surface. For some choice of local smoothing components, the criterion requires a relation on a crepant resolution among link classes whose associated local parameters avoid every discriminant. The complexified relation space describes first-order deformations modulo locally trivial ones. Necessity follows from local period and vanishing-cycle arguments; sufficiency applies Friedman's unobstructedness theorem to a crepant partial resolution. Whenever the criterion holds, the deformation space on the chosen components is smooth. A nonsmoothable example, whose deformation space is reduced with four smooth components, shows why nonvanishing at every singular point is insufficient. We also construct a smoothable Batyrev hypersurface admitting no smoothing induced by proper ambient families obtained from Minkowski decompositions at a single lattice degree.

title: There are no unexpected toric positroid varieties
abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a positroid. We prove that the positroid variety $Π_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to some algebraic torus if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is regular. In that case, $Π_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to the standard diagonal torus. Thus, there are no unexpected toric positroid varieties.

title: Bornologies and Kuratowski-Painlevé Convergence to the Empty Set Revisited
abstract: Let $(X,τ)$ be a noncompact metrizable space and let $\langle T_n\rangle$ be a sequence of nonempty closed sets converging to the empty set in the sense of Kuratowski--Painlevé. The subsets of $X$ whose closures meet at most finitely many terms form a bornology $\mathcal B_τ(\langle T_n\rangle)$. We give an internal criterion for inclusion between two such bornologies and recover each of them from a canonical free filter of closed sets. In fact, a nontrivial bornology is sequence-induced exactly when it has the enlargement property and its closed polar has countable character. Our principal result says that the bornology of relatively compact sets is sequence-induced precisely when $X$ is locally compact and separable; in the locally compact case the character of its closed polar is the density of $X$. In the penultimate section, we make a clever use of the sequence $T_n=\{n\}$ in the real line to give a negative answer to a conjecture posed in 2001 about a coarsest topology making the associated bornology a nontrivial metric bornology. Finally, we end the paper with a more general result: a coarsest such supertopology exists if and only if the original topology already makes the induced bornology a nontrivial metric bornology, in which case the coarsest supertopology is the original topology itself.

title: Soft normed linear spaces via soft elements: decomposition, convergence, and operators
abstract: Let $F\colon A\to\mathcal{P}(X)$ be a soft linear subspace of a linear space $X$ over $\mathbb{K}$. Its soft elements form the product $\prod_{t\in A}F(t)$. We use this representation to characterize selection spaces, decompose soft norms and soft linear operators into their sectionwise parts, and compare soft, uniform, and componentwise convergence. We also characterize completeness and continuity in the box, extended-supremum, and product settings. Neumann-series and fixed-point results are obtained as applications.

title: Countable models of one-dimensional Peano continua
abstract: In this paper, we prove that a one-dimensional Peano continuum $X$ admits a weak homotopy equivalence $X\to C$ to a countable space $C$ if and only if the wild set $\mathbf{w}(X)$ is countable.

title: Simultaneous Recovery of Wave Speeds and Initial Sources on Graphs via Redundant Frontier Propagation
abstract: We study the simultaneous recovery of an unknown initial signal and unknown vertex wave speeds for the wave equation on a finite graph from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we first show that a single experiment determines both quantities under a new two-witness zero forcing condition and generic nondegeneracy assumptions. We then develop a more general frontier-propagation framework in which the redundancy required for simultaneous recovery is distributed across successive graph contours rather than localized at individual forcing vertices. We derive Lipschitz stability estimates for the frontier propagation problem. We also show the recovery and stability results extend to positively weighted graphs.

title: Kwapień's property (K) in Lipschitz-free spaces
abstract: We prove that a Lipschitz-free space $\F(M)$ fails Kwapień's property (K) whenever its underlying metric space $M$ contains a bi-Lipschitz copy of $C\times K$, where $C\subset\R$ is closed with positive measure and $K$ contains a Cantor metric space. Consequently, this holds for every subset of $\R^n$, $n\geqslant2$, whose closure has positive measure, and for a compact planar set of Assouad dimension one. These Lipschitz-free spaces embed into no strongly weakly compactly generated space and no $L_1$-space; in the separable case their duals are not isomorphic to $\ell_\infty$. Combining our result with a decomposition of Aliaga and Medina, we show that $\F(\R^n\times\Z^m)$ is strongly weakly compactly generated if and only if it has (K), and this occurs precisely when $n\leqslant1$. In particular, $\F(\R^2)$ does not embed isomorphically into $\F(\R\times\Z)$, answering a question of Aliaga. The planar examples nevertheless have the Dunford--Pettis property and Pełczyński's property $(V^*)$ and are weakly sequentially complete.

title: From boundary geometry to counterexamples in Smale's mean value problem
abstract: This paper provides a human digestion of the recent counterexample to Smale's mean value problem found by GPT-6 Astra. We give a geometric mechanism for constructing counterexamples. An outward normal that re-enters an analytic Jordan domain, subject to a curvature condition, yields a holomorphic model whose normalized divided differences exceed one in modulus on the boundary. Polynomial perturbations then concentrate every critical point near the boundary whilst preserving the strict inequality. This turns boundary geometry into counterexamples in every sufficiently large degree. We also locate these critical points to first order and show that their limiting distribution is the logarithmic equilibrium measure on the boundary. We end with an explicit example of degree $29\,984$, verified by interval arithmetic.

title: A note on the Besov spaces ${\rm B}_1^{Φ_2}$
abstract: Regarding the Besov space ${\rm B}_1^{Φ_2}$, defined by S. Geiss and Ylinen (Memoirs AMS 1335, 2021) by a coupling method, we prove for $ξ\in{\rm B}_1^{Φ_2} \cap L_2$ a distributional estimate in terms of the Lorentz-Zygmund space $L_{1,\infty}(\ln L)^{-1}$ for the Malliavin derivative ${\rm D}(T_uξ)$ uniformly in $u>0$, where $(T_u)_{u\ge }$ is the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semi-group. Here $ξ$ is not necessarily Malliavin differentiable in the ${\rm D}_{1,1}$-sense. This provides for Theorem 4.22 of the aforementioned reference an extension to the borderline case $p=1$.

title: Fukaya categories of surfaces with DG coefficients
abstract:
Given a compact surface $S$ admitting a Liouville form, a finite set $Q \subset S$, a line field on $S$, and a local system of dg-categories on $S \setminus Q$ together with a section of the monodromy functor around each interior $q \in Q$, we construct a Fukaya category. We give examples where such Fukaya categories are quasi-equivalent to derived categories of projective completions of line bundles and of iterated blow-ups of the affine plane; and to wrapped Fukaya categories of cotangent bundles of spheres.
  We define two versions of the Fukaya category, a topological, which is constructed combinatorially from a full arc system, and a geometric, which includes all Lagrangian branes supported on immersed curves. We prove that the topological category embeds into the geometric category in an essentially unique way. To define Lagrangian branes we develop a generalisation of the Chekanov--Eliashberg algebra incorporating dg-coefficients and wrapping along the boundary.

title: A generalization of pseudocomplementation in semilattices, lattices and posets with 0
abstract: Pseudocomplemented lattices satisfy a lot of nice properties and were studied by a number of algebraists. However, even when a poset P with 0 is not pseudocomplemented, we can assign to every element a of P the set $a^p$ of all maximal elements being orthogonal to a. This assignment $^p$ is a non-trivial operator provided P satisfies the so-called Ascending Chain Condition (ACC). In particular, we investigate this operator when the poset P in question is a semilattice or a lattice. We characterize this operator and describe its properties that turn out to be similar to the corresponding properties of pseudocomplementation. Moreover, we introduce an equivalence relation $Θ_p$ on P induced by $^p$ similarly as it was done by V. I. Glivenko for distributive pseudocomplemented lattices. Finally, we investigate for which lattices L with 0 satisfying the ACC this equivalence relation turns out to be a congruence and when the quotient lattice $L/Θ_p$ is complemented respectively modular.

title: Average eccentricity in k-connected tournaments
abstract: The average eccentricity $\avec(D)$ of a strong digraph $D$ is the mean eccentricity of all vertices in $D$. A tournament $T$ is an orientation of a complete graph. In this paper, we prove that the average eccentricity satisfies $2 \le \avec(T) < \frac{n}{2k} + \frac{11}{2} + \frac{k}{8n}$ for a $k$-connected tournament $T$ of order $n$. We further examine the case for strong tournaments where $k = 1$, and show that $\avec(T) \le \frac{n+11}{2} + \frac{1}{8n}$ for any strong tournament $T$. Moreover, we show that the lower bound $2$ is sharp and that the upper bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant.

title: On the frieze patterns by Conway and Coxeter
abstract: The story of frieze patterns started in 1970s with a paper by Coxeter and two short papers by Conway and Coxeter, one listing questions and the other providing brief answers. During the first three decades it was followed by only a handful of papers observing some further properties of the same objects. Then Propp (2005) and Caldero and Chapoton (2006) established connections between frieze patterns and the recent theory of cluster algebras introduced by Fomin and Zelevinsky in early 2000s. Since then the theory of frieze patterns exploded with new results, and frieze patterns found a wide spectrum of connections in various domains of mathematics, including combinatorics, geometry, representation theory and integrable systems. The literature on frieze patterns grew vastly and continues to expand. In this note we give a brief overview of some of the directions emerging from the papers by Conway and Coxeter and single out core ideas which were later replayed in different contexts.

title: A Separated Bump Theorem in $L^2$
abstract: We prove a separated entropy bump theorem for two-weight $L^2$ inequalities for positive operators defined by Carleson sequences on a probability space with a general filtration. The bump conditions use conditional averages of martingale maximal functions and involve the first power of the entropy penalty, removing the square appearing in the separated condition of Treil and Volberg. As a consequence, we obtain separated Orlicz bump estimates for a class of doubling Young functions. These results apply, in particular, to sparse operators. The proof uses principal sequences, a natural global extension of principal sets, and combines a good-$λ$ estimate with a weighted Carleson embedding to obtain the required testing inequalities.

title: On Thom Polynomials for $\mathcal{A}$-singularities of parametric curves and degeneracy loci formulas
abstract: In this research article, we make an in-depth investigation of the computations for Thom Polynomials for $\mathcal{A}$-singularities of parametric curves germs in the plane and space cases using the framework established by Ohmoto and the Restriction Method introduced by Rimányi, and we also propose a geometric way for such computations using degeneracy loci Chern classes formulas proven by Fulton, which seems a promising way to generalize the Thom Polynomial expression for the stabilization of such singularities in $\mathbb{C}^N$, depending exclusively on $N$ as a parameter.

title: Geometric priors for single-patch neural Calabi--Yau metrics on the quintic: a conservative fixed-$ψ$ Ablation study
abstract: We investigate how geometric priors shape neural approximations of the complex Monge--Amp`ere equation on the quintic Calabi--Yau threefold. This fixed-$ψ$ diagnostic compares four single-patch ans"atze: a coordinate SIREN potential model, a direct-metric Cholesky baseline, an algebraic section ansatz, and a section-plus-neural hybrid. In a 96-run learning-rate and frequency archive, section-based models reach validation $σ=4.14$--$4.16%$, whereas SIREN and Cholesky remain at $41.29%$ and $44.27%$. Multi-seed controls use a shared affine-$η$ evaluator and five fresh validation clouds. Stable section settings give $3.84$--$4.77%$, compared with $28.46$--$30.59%$ for Cholesky and $34.73$--$38.13%$ for SIREN. Hybrid projective features do not improve best-case accuracy, but they stabilise the stressed regime. They limit $σ$ to $4.26$--$4.41%$, versus $4.45$--$205.45%$ for raw coordinates. Within this protocol, section-based geometric structure is the main driver of accuracy; coordinate-only models plateau at substantially higher error, and raw hybrid flexibility can amplify instability. We provide a projective-scaling derivation, document protocol asymmetries, and identify projectively consistent hybrid corrections as the next step.

title: Motivic $C_p$-power operations in $\mathrm{MGL}$
abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of the Hopkins-Morel-Hoyois theorem for fields $k$ of characteristic unequal to $p$ containing all primitive $p$-power roots of unity for a fixed prime $p$. This new proof follows Quillen's proof for the structure of the homotopy groups of $\mathrm{MU}$ which utilizes topological power operations. To this end we define a motivic analog of the Steenrod power operations, using the theory of normed motivic spectra as developed by Bachmann--Hoyois and their application for the definition of motivic colimits as developed by Bachmann-Elmanto-Heller.

title: Algebraic properties of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel operators
abstract: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of $\mathcal{S}_θ$---the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space $\mathcal{K}_θ$. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators under certain conditions. As applications, we describe the non-uniqueness of a decomposition $T=A+B$, show that self-adjoint operators admit self-adjoint decompositions, give a necessary and sufficient inclusion criterion for $\mathcal{S}_θ$ when $θ$ is a finite Blaschke product, and, from a first-order commutator characterization of $\mathcal{S}_θ$, describe the products of its elements and the operators commuting with $S_θ+ S_θ^{*}$.

title: A Radon-Nikodým theorem for Fuzzy Number Multimeasures in Locally Convex Spaces
abstract: In this paper, we present a Radon-Nikodym theorem for dominated fuzzy number multimeasures defined on $Σ$ and taking values in $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$, where $(Ω, Σ, μ)$ is a complete finite measure space and $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$ is the family of generalized fuzzy numbers on a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space $X$, i.e., a map $u: X \to [0,1]$ is a member of $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$, if and only if for each $α\in (0,1]$ the $α$-cut $[u]^α$ of $u$ is a member of the family $cwk(X)$ of all nonempty convex and weakly compact subsets of $X$, ($[u]^α = \{x \in X: u(x) \geq α\}$).

title: A Counterexample to a Bourgain-Brezis Sum-Space Estimate
abstract: A question of Bourgain and Brezis, later restated as Open Problem 7.1 by Brezis, asks whether the $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ norm of a mean-zero scalar function is controlled by the ambient $H^{-1/2}+L^1$ sum norm of its gradient. We show that this estimate fails in every dimension $N\geq 2$. More precisely, for every integer $K\geq 16$, we construct a smooth real-valued mean-zero function $Φ_K$ on $\mathbb{T}^N$ such that $|\nablaΦ_K|{H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+L^1(\mathbb{T}^N)}\leq C$ and $|Φ_K|{H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)}\geq cK^{1/4}-C$, where the absolute constants $c,C>0$ are independent of $N$ and $K$. Equivalently, the ratio of the gradient-constrained decomposition cost to the ambient decomposition cost is unbounded. The construction applies the Hodge projection to a smooth approximation of a normal vector measure on a codimension-one sheet. Its potential records lacunary partial sums at geometrically separated distances from the sheet. A scale-path lower bound, combined with an odd critical Hardy inequality, excludes uniformly bounded $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ decompositions.

title: A functional model for hyponormal contractions
abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical model for a class of hyponormal contractions $T$ satisfying $Ran[T^*,T] \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}\ominus \mathcal D_T$, where $\mathcal D_{T^*}$ and $\mathcal D_T$ are the associated defect spaces for $T$. We also show that, under a certain condition, a contraction $T$ with $\mathcal D_T \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}$ is hyponormal.

title: There Are Exactly $2^\mathfrak{c}$ Simultaneously Bireflective and Bicoreflective Subconstructs of $\mathbf{FTS}$
abstract: We prove that there are exactly $2^\mathfrak{c}$ simultaneously bireflective and bicoreflective subconstructs of $\mathbf{FTS}$. By the Lowen--Wuyts bijection, these correspond to the total fuzzy topologies contained in $M$, the fuzzy topology consisting of all nondecreasing left-continuous self-maps of the unit interval. The upper bound follows from a cardinality estimate. The matching lower bound is obtained by encoding $2^{\mathfrak c}$ ultrafilters on $\mathbb N$ into total fuzzy topologies contained in $M$.

title: Characterizing $3$-graphs with Degenerate Codegree Turán Density
abstract:
Determining the Turán densities $π(F)$, uniform Turán densities $π_{\therefore}(F)$, and codegree Turán densities $γ(F)$ of $3$-graphs $F$ is a notoriously difficult problem in combinatorics. A landmark result by Erdős characterized the $3$-graphs whose Turán density is zero. Half a century later, Reiher, Rödl, and Schacht characterized the $3$-graphs whose uniform Turán density is zero. Recently, Ding, Lamaison, Liu, Wang, and Yang suggested a possible characterization of $3$-graphs whose codegree Turán density is zero, proved one direction of it, and conjectured the other. In this work we confirm this conjecture, completing the characterization of $3$-graphs with codegree Turán density zero. A particular difficulty of this result is that it is known that there are $3$-graphs with arbitrarily small codegree Turán density, contrasting the behavior of the normal and the uniform Turán density.
  Similar results were independently announced by Chen, Fang, and Yang.

title: Cops and Robbers on Graphs without Long or Short Holes
abstract: In 2019, Sivaraman conjectured that every $P_k$-free graph has cop number at most $k-3$ for $k\geq 5$. Chudnovsky, Norin, Seymour, and Turcotte proved $P_5$-free graphs have cop number at most $2$. For $k\geq 6$ Sivaraman's conjecture remains widely open. There is little evidence to believe Sivaraman's conjecture is optimal, making the discovery of substantially better bounds interesting, even for subclasses of $P_k$-free graphs. We consider this problem for graphs with no long holes, which generalizes $P_k$-free graphs, that also have some forbidden shorter holes. Specifically, we show that for $t\geq 13$, $(C_4,\dots, C_{t}, C_k,C_{k+1},\dots)$-free graphs have cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-2}{\lfloor \frac{t}{4}\rfloor }\rceil+1$. Taking $C_{k-1}$, which has cop number $2$ whenever $k\geq 5$, demonstrates that this bound is tight up to a small constant factor for infinity many pairs $k$ and $t$. The proof relies on showing that in graphs without short holes, the closed neighbourhood of a short induced path can be guarded by $1$ cop, even when these paths are not geodesics. Additionally, for $t\geq 2$ we show that $(C_{t+2},C_{t+3},C_k, C_{k+1},\dots, )$-free graphs have cop number at most $(t-1)\lceil \frac{(k-2)}{t}\rceil$. This show that $(C_4,C_5,C_k,C_{k+1},\dots)$-free graphs have cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-2}{2}\rceil$, extending work by Clow and Meger on $(P_k,\text{claw}, \text{butterfly}, C_4,C_5)$-free graphs to a substantially more general class.

title: BV structure on the Hochschild cohomology of Liu-Schulz algebras in characteristic two
abstract: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $2$, let $ρ\in K^\times$, and let $R_ρ$ be the corresponding Liu-Schulz algebra. We give a complete description of the Gerstenhaber bracket and the BV structure on the Hochschild cohomology ring $\operatorname{HH}^*(R_ρ)$.

title: On the existence of polarized varieties without weakly Ulrich bundles
abstract: We give an obstruction to the existence of bundles $\mathcal E$ on a smooth $n$-dimensional polarized variety such that $\mathcal E$ is $a$-regular and ${\mathcal E}^*(K_X+(n+1)H)$ is $b$-regular. In particular, this gives an obstruction to the existence of weakly Ulrich bundles. Using the latter and some recent examples of [A1] in dimension $2$, we prove that for any $n \ge 2$ there exist many smooth $n$-dimensional varieties $X$ with a very ample line bundle $H$, such that there is no weakly Ulrich bundle for $(X,H)$.

title: Explicit Reed-Solomon Subspace Designs: Optimal List and Line Decoding
abstract:
For any desired rate $R \in (0,1)$, and gap to list-decoding capacity $\varepsilon > 0$, we give an explicit $n^{O_{\varepsilon}(1)}$ time construction of Reed-Solomon codes over extension fields of size polynomial in the block length $n$ that can be list-decoded from a fraction $1-R-\varepsilon$ of errors with the optimal list-size of $O(\frac{1-R}{\varepsilon})$. We also give a simpler, strongly explicit construction of evaluation points for which the associated Reed-Solomon code can be list-decoded from $1-R-\varepsilon$ errors with list size $(1/\varepsilon)^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$. We provide a deterministic list-decoding algorithm for both constructions running in time $O_ε(1)\mathsf{poly}(n)$.
  In fact, our Reed-Solomon codes are near-optimal subspace-design codes over a subfield. Via known results, this directly implies the combinatorial list-decoding guarantee, as well as near-optimal list-recovery bounds. We also present a new reduction showing that the subspace-design guarantee also implies line decoding over the extension field itself, which then yields proximity gaps and mutual correlated agreement up to proximity parameter approaching the optimal $1-R$ radius.
  Compared to the recent algorithm of Brakensiek, Chen, Putterman, Zhang, and Zheng (2026), which list decodes every Reed-Solomon code over prime fields up to capacity, our approach achieves constant (in fact, near-optimal) list size rather than a polynomially growing one, at the cost of carefully choosing the code's evaluation points. In a companion paper, we show that these respective restrictions are unavoidable.

title: Contact topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms
abstract: We study the geometry and topology of transversely vanishing eigenforms of the curl operator on $3$-manifolds, placing them in the broader framework of near-contact forms. We prove a Gray-type stability theorem for the kernels of near-contact forms, which we call near-contact structures, and derive a local neighborhood theorem around their singularities. As applications, we obtain a stability result for the contact topology of curl eigenforms, a classification of near-contact structures in terms of formal homotopical data, and a proof of the existence of contact structures on closed orientable 3-manifolds based on the spectral theory of the curl operator. We also study the symplectization of curl eigenforms as a possible bridge to symplectic dynamics. Finally, we characterize those transversely vanishing $1$-forms which are curl eigenforms for some smooth Riemannian metric. We deduce a generalization of the classical correspondence, due to Etnyre and Ghrist, between Reeb-like fields of contact forms and nowhere-vanishing rotational Beltrami fields to the setting of transversely vanishing vector fields.

title: Stability analysis of the Lane--Emden equation of index $n=5$ describing polytropic gas spheres
abstract: We study the Lane--Emden equation of index $n=5$, the critical polytropic case separating finite-radius from infinite-radius self-gravitating equilibria. The scaling family $θ_λ(ξ)=λ^{1/2}θ(λξ)$ generates a neutral mode $φ_0=\tfrac12θ+ξθ'$ about the Schuster profile. Schuster's transformation and a logarithmic variable reduce the equation to the autonomous Hamiltonian system $\ddotν=\tfrac14(ν-ν^5)$ with a first integral. Besides the Schuster (separatrix) and Srivastava solutions, every orbit crossing $ν=0$ is given in closed form by a Weierstrass $\wp$-function, and the closed forms agree with direct numerical integration to about $10^{-12}$. Up to scaling and sign, the Schuster solution is the only solution regular at the center, and it separates positive solutions from solutions with infinitely many zeros. In homology-invariant variables the singular solution $θ=(2ξ)^{-1/2}$ is a center exactly at $n=5$, where its stability changes. For a distance-varying Emden--Fowler system with a shifted equilibrium we prove that at $n=5$ the unique equilibrium is linearly and nonlinearly unstable. Finally, the linearization about the Schuster profile is the Schrödinger operator $L=-Δ_r-5θ_S^4$ on $L^2((0,\infty),ξ^2dξ)$. Its Friedrichs extension has essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$, a threshold resonance at $0$ carried by the non-normalizable scaling mode, and exactly one negative eigenvalue, $λ_0\approx-1.21$, so the Schuster profile is a saddle point of the associated energy functional.

title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.

title: Nonvanishing implies abundance
abstract: We prove that the nonvanishing conjecture implies the abundance conjecture.

title: A vanishing-cycle obstruction to smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds
abstract: We prove a homological obstruction to smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees six and seven. On a crepant resolution that is small over the nodes and blows up the cone vertices, any smoothing forces a relation among link classes bounding in the local Milnor fibers. The relation is nonzero at every node and degree-seven point, and at each degree-six point smoothed through the one-dimensional component. The proof uses vanishing periods and applies to smoothing arcs of arbitrary contact order, extending the necessity direction of Friedman's criterion. We apply the obstruction to a Batyrev hypersurface whose thirty singularities are individually smoothable but which admits no smoothing, even formally. On its mirror partner, two nodes cannot be smoothed by any analytic deformation, independently of a locally nonsmoothable cone point.

title: Closed Lindelöf $Σ$ Kernels of Neighborhood Assignments in Charming Spaces
abstract: Every neighborhood assignment on a charming space $X$ has a countable kernel whose closure in $X$ is Lindelöf $Σ$. Consequently, for any two neighborhood assignments $M$ and $N$ on $X$, there is a closed discrete set $D\subseteq X$ such that $M[N[D]]=X$. We give an exact one-step formulation of the remaining $D$-space problem and identify the universal pointwise square-refinement condition with the classical $z$-space condition. For continuous closed surjections, we prove a fixed-assignment lifting equivalence. We also show that every uncountable $\mathrm{HFC}_{\mathrm w}$ subspace of $[ω_1]^{\leqω}$ is dually closed countable but not charming. For a fixed Lindelöf $Σ$ kernel $Y$, we iterate the Hu--Yin boundary reduction by a transfinite closed-core process. At every stage, the current iterate is a $D$-space if and only if $X$ is a $D$-space. The iteration stabilizes before $hL(Y)^+$ at the largest closed subspace in which the kernel trace and its complement are both dense. The bound is sharp: for every infinite cardinal $κ$ and every $γ<κ^+$, there is a compact example with a dense $σ$-compact Lindelöf $Σ$ kernel $Y$ satisfying $hL(Y)=|Y|=κ$ whose first stabilization stage is $γ$.

title: Elementary Moves on Ideal Webs, Local Monodromies on Hitchin Fibrations, and Tropical Mutations on $\mathrm{K_0}$ Groups
abstract:
This paper builds on the work of Goncharov by studying the correspondence between topological spectral covers constructed from generic $A_{m-1}$-webs with rank $m\ge2$, Hitchin spectral curves over good Hitchin loci, and the Grothendieck groups $K_0(\mathcal{D}_Γ)$ associated with the quivers with potential $(Q_Γ,W_Γ)$ assigned to corresponding bipartite $A_{m-1}$-graphs.
  We show that the automorphisms on the non-frozen quiver lattices $Λ_Γ^{\circ}$ induced by compositions of elementary moves on ideal webs/bipartite graphs are the same as the Gauss--Manin monodromy actions on the $SL_m$ Hitchin fiber lattices $H_1(\operatorname{Prym}(Σ);\mathbb{Z})$ locally around discriminant loci. And the Gauss--Manin monodromy actions agree with the automorphisms on the Grothendieck groups $K_0(\mathcal{D}_Γ^{\circ})$ induced by compositions of mutations on the quivers with potential $(Q_Γ,W_Γ)$.

title: Accelerating Langevin Dynamics with Weighted Laplacian Flow: Global Well-Posedness and Exponential Convergence
abstract: We study an accelerated Langevin equation in which the classical overdamped Langevin drift is supplemented by a nonlocal gradient velocity determined through a target-weighted Poisson equation. The target $p$ is only assumed to be strictly positive and need not be normalized. Writing the dynamics in terms of $ω=\log(p/q)$ yields a coupled parabolic-elliptic system whose parabolic component contains the usual Langevin diffusion, whereas the elliptic component generates a global transport. The system is invariant under multiplication of $p$ by a positive constant. On a bounded smooth domain with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, we establish global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for strictly positive $C^{2+α}$ target weights and compatible $C^{2+α}$ initial data. For long-time behavior, the oscillation of $ω$ decays at the explicit rate $e^{-t}$ and the solution density exponentially converges to target density. Moreover, an exact entropy-dissipation identity holds relative to the target density, in which the relative Fisher information and the Jeffreys divergence give the two dissipation mechanisms associated with the Langevin and weighted-Poisson components. In particular, KL divergence also converges to zero with rate $e^{-t}$ without a convexity assumption on the target.

title: Observable diameter of product measures with a power-type interior zero
abstract: We determine the asymptotic order of the observable diameter of $\ell^p$-product spaces associated with a probability measure on $[0,1]$ whose density has a power-type interior zero. Different vanishing orders are allowed on the two sides of the zero. For every $1 \le p \le \infty$, we obtain sharp two-sided estimates and show that the asymptotic order is governed by the larger of the two vanishing orders. In the case $p=2$, the transition occurs exactly at the threshold for the spectral gap.

title: Quaternionic Buzano-Dragomir Inequality and Deutsch Entropic Uncertainty Principle
abstract: We show that the Buzano-Dragomir inequality holds for quaternionic Hilbert spaces. Using this generalization, we derive the Dragomir inequality for the quaternionic numerical radius and Deutsch entropic uncertainty principle for quaternionic Hilbert spaces.

title: On the Luxemburg Functional in the Concave Regime with an Application to Nonlocal Differential Equations
abstract: For $p:[0,1]\to(0,1)$ a continuous function, we consider the Luxemburg functional \[ Λ_{p(\cdot)}(u):=\inf\left\{δ>0:\int_0^1\left|\frac{u(t)}δ\right|^{p(t)}\,dt\leq 1\right\}. \] We develop a suitable functional analytic framework for $Λ_{p(\cdot)}$ so that it can be incorporated into a positive order cone, which can then be used in the analysis of nonlocal differential equations having the general form \[ -A\left(\int_0^1 b(1-s)(u(s))^{p(s)}\,ds\right)u''(t) =λf(t,u(t)),\qquad t\in(0,1). \] By means of a specific numerical example, we demonstrate that, as opposed to a methodology relying only on the supremum norm, our methodology via the Luxemburg functional yields an appreciably sharper localisation of any solutions of the nonlocal equation.

title: Pointwise to global good reduction problems
abstract: Given a smooth proper family of varieties over some $p$-adic field, if (sufficiently many of) the closed fibers have good reduction, does the family as a whole have good reduction? This question is asked and positively answered in recent work of Cadoret-Tamagawa for curves in general, and abelian varieties if the base field has absolute ramification at most $p-1$. In this paper we define a general framework for studying this question, yielding new positive answers for families of K3 surfaces and cubic fourfoulds, again with ramification at most $p-1$. Our strategy is to study several extension properties of moduli spaces and how they transfer under various morphisms. Of particular importance are integral canonical models of Shimura varieties, and whether or not their extension properties are preserved under ramified scalar extension. Additionally, building on earlier counterexamples by Raynaud-Ogus-Gabber and Vasiu-Zink, we show that the ramification assumption is optimal for the result of Cadoret-Tamagawa on families of abelian varieties. This reflects the fact that the extension property of Siegel Shimura varieties no longer holds over a field of absolute ramification at least $p$.

title: A unified family of multiblock ADMM schemes by means of graph splitting
abstract: This paper introduces a novel unified family of multiblock ADMM schemes by combining Gabay duality with a graph-based splitting methodology. This framework allows us to recover existing ADMM algorithms as particular instances, as well as to generate new ones by varying the underlying network topology. We focus specifically on the case of the complete graph, a structure of significant practical interest due to its dense connectivity, for which we provide a fully explicit and directly implementable scheme. We further derive an equivalent reformulation of the proposed family in which the algorithm is expressed in terms of a reduced set of dual variables, which clarifies its connection to the classical ADMM framework. Numerical experiments are conducted to compare the performance of different graph choices, showing particularly favorable results for the complete graph.

title: Edge complexity of complete bipartite and complete multipartite graphs
abstract: We study edge complexity, the minimum Fourier $\ell^1/\ell^2$ ratio of a graph's adjacency matrix over cyclic vertex labelings. For $K_{m,n}$, with $1\leq m\leq n$, we reduce the problem to minimizing the Fourier $\ell^1$-norm of indicators of $m$-element subsets of $\mathbb Z_{m+n}$. We prove the sharp bound $\operatorname{FR}_{\min}(K_{m,n})\geq\frac{4n^2}{(m+n)\sqrt{2mn}}$, with equality precisely when $m\mid n$, and classify all labelings attaining it. We determine all Fourier ratios and minimizing labelings for $K_{2,n}$, and all minimizing labelings for $K_{3,n}$. Put $N=n+3$. The optimal three-element sets are precisely the cosets of the subgroup of order $3$ in $\mathbb Z_N$ when $3\mid N$, and precisely the arithmetic progressions with invertible common difference otherwise. The triple classification uses polynomial minorants and additive energies. We prove that attainment of the graph-energy bound is invariant under uniform independent set blow-ups. Edge complexity itself can decrease by an arbitrarily large factor under a twofold blow-up, and we give a finite example. For complete multipartite graphs, we give an exact labeling formula and sharp lower bound, and classify all part sizes and labelings attaining that bound. This bound strictly improves the graph-energy bound when the part sizes are unequal. We prove a lower bound for arbitrary simple graphs in terms of their average degree and maximum absolute degree deviation. For Laplacian projectors, we apply the equality criterion for the multiplicity bound to unbalanced complete bipartite graphs, whose top-projector minimum reduces to the same set minimization. Finally, we apply existing Fourier recovery and sampling theorems to approximate a graph from random adjacency samples under a fixed known labeling with bounded Fourier ratio, bounding the number of incorrectly recovered edges.

title: Infinite families and sporadic solutions of the equation $\varphi(n)=c+α\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi(p)$
abstract: Ranjan and Singh proved that for every composite $n$ which is not twice an odd prime, $\varphi(n)$ is at least one plus the sum of $\varphi$ over the prime divisors of $n$, with equality exactly for $n=4,12,30$. \new{We study the weighted equation $\varphi(n)=c+α\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi(p)$. We determine the parameters $(c,α)$ admitting infinite families of solutions, prove that all remaining solutions are finite in number and arise from an explicit linear mechanism, and compute them exactly in a range of parameters; the finiteness of $\{4,12,30\}$ becomes a special case. We also settle the analogous equations for the divisor functions $τ$ and $σ$ and for the Jordan totients, and, from known results on the sum of the prime divisors, derive the full asymptotic expansion of the average deficiency.} \K{In the range $|c|\le10$, $1\leα\le6$ the composite solution set is determined completely\V{, and the number and the size of the sporadic solutions are shown to be bounded by polynomials in $|c|+α$}.} \B{Finally, replacing the prime values $\varphi(p)$ by their iterates $\varphi^{(k)}(p)$, we determine all solutions of $\varphi(n)=1+\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi^{(k)}(p)$: the solution sets are $\{1,4,12,30\}$, $\{1,3,4,10\}$ and, for every $k\ge3$, $\{1,3,4\}$; for the weighted iterated equation we exhibit an infinite family governed by the safe primes.

title: Dynamical Tensor Train Approximation for Wigner--Fokker--Planck Equation with Applications to Open Quantum Systems
abstract: We develop a dynamical tensor-train method for the Wigner--Fokker--Planck equation arising in continuous-variable open quantum systems. The Wigner function is evolved directly in tensor-train form using a projector-splitting integrator, while the nonlocal Wigner pseudo-differential operator is treated through low-rank representations of the potential difference and matrix-free exponential actions. The resulting method avoids full tensor-product computations in high-dimensional phase space. Numerical experiments in one, two, and three spatial dimensions demonstrate the accuracy and scalability of the method, including simulations in a six-dimensional phase space.

title: Cost benefits of designing carbon capture processes for part-load operation of power plants
abstract: As fossil power plants increasingly cycle to balance variable renewable generation, carbon capture plants must be designed for a wide range of part-load operating conditions, to avoid excessive capital costs. However, accounting for the variability in design optimization yields higher computational complexity, and is therefore not a current design methodology. Here, we apply two-stage stochastic optimization to identify optimal carbon capture plant designs accounting for part-load flue gas conditions. We reduce computational complexity through a data-driven approach-to-equilibrium model of the absorption and desorption processes. Operating scenarios are derived from real-world part-load operation data of coal and natural gas combined cycle power plants. Our results demonstrate that designs optimized over multiple operating scenarios substantially reduce equipment sizes, lowering capital costs by 5-9 % at the expense of higher operating costs, resulting in a moderate reduction in total annualized cost by 0.5-1.6 %. The lowest costs are achieved when targeting an average capture target across operating scenarios, which allows CO2 capture to be shifted from full-load to part-load periods to reduce peak equipment sizes without compromising overall CO2 emission reductions. These cost benefits are robust across sensitivity analyses and increase with higher shares of part-load operation. Thus, part-load variability should be considered at the design stage, particularly for plants subject to variable load.

title: Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings of Minimal Order
abstract: A ring $R$ with non-zero identity element is said to be centrally essential if for any non-zero element $a$ of $R$, there exist non-zero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In the paper, we prove that the minimal order of a finite non-commutative centrally essential ring is equal to $64$. A partial classification of such rings is presented, and the existence of non-isomorphic non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order is proved.

title: Universal Critical Jump for Inverse-Square Ising Ferromagnets
abstract: For every translation-invariant ferromagnetic Ising chain with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, we prove $2β_cBm_c^2=1$, without restrictions on the finite core or the tail convergence rate. The proof bounds the energy of macroscopic interfaces and rules them out if the critical product exceeds one. Despite the nonzero jump, connected susceptibility is infinite both at criticality and in a neighboring ordered interval. At the critical coupling, the excess magnetization decays more slowly than any positive power of the field as the field tends to zero. We also prove the jump relation in continuous time, for a positive-Stieltjes class of Ohmic spin-boson models.

title: Uniform local models of quasi-unipotent $p$-adic differential equations
abstract: We construct uniform analytic models of quasi-unipotent differential modules over Robba rings. For modules of rank at most $r$ and highest ramification break at most $b$, the inner radius of the model annulus depends only on $r,b$ and the residue characteristic $p$. At each radius, the model admits a basis, possibly depending on the radius, in which the connection matrix is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,b,p$. Both bounds are independent of the coefficient field, and these analytic models require no coefficient extension. A prescribed absolute Frobenius structure extends to such a bounded model with the same radius and connection bound. After a finite coefficient extension, we also realize quasi-constant modules, which carry the finite local monodromy, as differential direct summands of sums of pushforwards of rank-one modules, with uniformly bounded cover degrees and highest breaks of the inducing modules.

title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the McShane-Rivin unit ball.

title: Rigidity and Affine Deformations of Foliations on Nilpotent and Solvable Contact Lie Algebras
abstract: Let g be a Lie algebra of dimension 2n+1, let beta be a contact form, and let alpha be a nonzero integrable 1-form. We study when the affine path alpha_t = (1-t)alpha + t beta consists of contact forms with the orientation determined by beta \wedge (d beta)^n. We first establish an algebraic criterion: affine deformability is equivalent to the non-negativity of a scalar obtained from the interaction form Theta(alpha, beta) = alpha \wedge (d beta)^n + n beta \wedge d alpha \wedge (d beta)^{n-1}. For unimodular Lie algebras this scalar is (n+1)alpha(Z_beta), where Z_beta is the Reeb vector. We also derive a formula involving the modular character tau(X) = tr(ad_X) in the non-unimodular case. On nilpotent contact Lie algebras, every integrable 1-form is closed; using the standard structural properties of nilpotent contact Lie algebras, this implies that every left-invariant foliation is an affine origin for every fixed contact form. An explicit three-dimensional example illustrates that the modular term can yield affine deformability even when alpha(Z_beta) = 0. We discuss the implications for left-invariant forms on Lie groups and compact quotients. We do not claim a general obstruction example in the non-unimodular case; establishing such an example requires a separate verified construction.

title: A direct proof of Infinity in NF-0
abstract: We give a direct proof of Infinity in the no-empty version of New Foundations, denoted NF-0, by establishing that every model of the specified theory contains an object that is not finite in a precise, internally defined sense. The version considered has extensionality, at least two distinct objects, no empty objects, and inhabited stratified comprehension: a stratified extension is supplied whenever it has a member. Finiteness combines a two-sided internally represented well-order with the exclusion of internally represented nonterminating strict transitive relations on inhabited subsets. Assuming all objects finite, partial bijections yield comparison and finite extrema of positive Frege cardinals. Positive exponentiation, singleton type-raising, and the least orbit of the genuine two-cardinal lead to the equation n = T(n) + 1. We prove separately, and in detail, that adjoining one point reverses internally defined parity: the key ingredients are a graph-rewiring proof of invariance under adjoining two points and one instance of stratified induction derived from the all-finite assumption. Since type-raising preserves parity, the cardinal equation is impossible. We identify the corresponding Lean 4 declarations and make explicit the scope of the formal verification. No model-existence or consistency theorem for ordinary NF is claimed.

title: University Research and Leadership in the Age of AI: Mobilizing Intellectual Capacity and Building the Infrastructure for Discovery
abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) raise the prospect of substantial changes in how research is conducted and who can direct discovery. This perspective argues that universities should prepare for these changes by developing AI as well as using it, rather than relying primarily on capabilities designed elsewhere. The relationship is reciprocal: AI can advance disciplinary research, while scientific questions, experimental evidence, and observed failures can guide AI development. The proposal distinguishes three complementary commitments: shared operation of existing AI models, disciplinary AI development, and foundational AI research. Their resource requirements differ, and no single university needs to reproduce a frontier AI company. Shared computational services should be connected to sustained technical teams, laboratory experimentation, and knowledge records that make findings traceable and reusable. Independent evaluation, alignment research, transparent resource allocation, and inclusive academic governance are integral to this infrastructure. Consortia and national facilities can support capabilities beyond individual campuses while preserving room for investigator-led inquiry. Initial programs in experimental and mathematical research would test scientific value, the effort required to validate results, and improvements to AI before expansion. The argument concerns research rather than educational reform and calls for building institutional capacity before the extent and timing of disruption are settled.

title: Two-sided logarithmic estimates of the Lebesgue constants with respect to Vilenkin systems
abstract: We introduce a new logarithmic digit variation for Vilenkin--Fourier partial sums and establish two-sided estimates for the corresponding Lebesgue constants with universal constants. These estimates hold for both bounded and unbounded Vilenkin systems.
