As an application, we show that bounded logarithmic variation yields uniform boundedness of the corresponding partial-sum operators on \(L_1\), \(L_1\)-norm convergence for every integrable function, and almost everywhere convergence.

title: Exact $L^2$ convergence through the wavelet and tent space characterizations of $h^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $0<p\le 1$
abstract: We extend the wavelet and tent space characterization of $h^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ to $0<p\le 1$ via a local dyadic tent space $t_p$, and derive the unconditional $L^2$-convergence of the resulting atomic decomposition, with an exact error identity refining Ding, Jiang and Zhu (2019).

title: Boundary and Interior of Root Sets of Power Series
abstract: In this paper we study the set $\mathcal{M}_M$ of roots of power series with coefficients in $\{0, \pm 1, ..., \pm M \}$ and constant coefficient $1$. We prove that every nonreal root in the unit disk of a polynomial of this form is an interior point of $\mathcal{M}_M$. Moreover we establish a dimension formula and show the corresponding Hausdorff measure is finite and positive for a family of attractors parameterized by boundary parameters $λ\in \partial \mathcal{M}_M \setminus \mathbb{R}$. Finally we show that $\partial \mathcal{M}_M$ has Lebesgue measure zero.

title: On various notions of universally Baire sets and reflection of non-Baire property in Cantor sets
abstract:
Universally Baire sets are a standard tool in modern set theory, where they are closely connected with forcing and absoluteness. In this paper we study universal Baireness instead as purely a regularity notion for subsets of Polish spaces. Our aim is not to develop the set-theoretic theory, but to place the notion on a systematic descriptive-set-theoretic footing and to clarify the several nonequivalent definitions that occur in the literature.
  A subset of a Polish space is called \emph{universally Baire} if all its continuous preimages possess the property of Baire. However, it is important to specify what the domain of these continuous functions can be. In fact, a plethora of definitions are used by various authors in the literature, the class of possible domains is sometimes the class of Polish spaces, compact metrizable spaces, all topological spaces, compact topological spaces, etc.
  We clarify this situation by demonstrating that the above four options are pairwise nonequivalent under the Continuum Hypothesis, we determine all the implications between these four notions that are provable in $ZFC$, and also show that all the notions used in the literature are equivalent to one of these four.
  Furthermore, we use Miller forcing to show that actually the cases of Polish and compact metrizable spaces are consistently equivalent.
  We show that numerous definitions using Borel isomorphisms, changes of topologies and Boolean algebras are all equivalent to the case of Polish domains.
  We present an argument that the notion using Polish domains is the natural dual to the notion of universally measurable sets.
  Finally, as a byproduct, we prove that the following statement is independent of $ZFC$: if a subset of a Polish space has the property of Baire relative to every nowhere dense Cantor subspace, then the subset has the property of Baire in the whole space.

title: Proximal Point Newton Methods for Nonconvex Optimization
abstract: Tensor methods offer improved complexity guarantees for nonconvex optimization, but evaluating high-order derivatives and solving the corresponding subproblems can be computationally expensive. In this paper, we develop a proximal point Newton framework that exploits third-derivative smoothness using only gradients and Hessians. Under Hessian Lipschitz continuity, a single-loop proximal point Newton method that alternates between negative-curvature directions and Newton steps finds an $(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)$-approximate second-order stationary point within $\mathcal{O}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-3/2},\varepsilon_H^{-3}\})$ second-order oracle evaluations. When the third derivative is also Lipschitz continuous, we introduce an accelerated proximal point Newton method and obtain a dimension-free complexity of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-4/3},\varepsilon_H^{-2}\})$, matching that of the third-order tensor methods up to logarithmic factors without constructing tensors or solving tensor subproblems. We further develop an adaptive inexact Newton--CG variant that requires no prior knowledge of Lipschitz constants and preserves the improved oracle complexity with high probability. Under uniformly bounded queried Hessians, this variant achieves a Hessian-vector product complexity of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-5/3},\varepsilon_H^{-5/2}\})$, improving upon the previous $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-3}\varepsilon_H^{5/2},\varepsilon_H^{-7/2}\})$ result attained by existing second-order methods such as cubic regularized Newton method and Newton--CG method. Preliminary numerical experiments are encouraging.

title: The Calderón problem for the fractional Schrödinger equation at a single point
abstract: We revisit the Calderón problem for the fractional Schrödinger equation and prove that the potential is determined by Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps at a single exterior point, with exterior inputs varying in a disjoint open set. This holds for continuous potentials for all $0<s<1$ and for bounded potentials when $s\geq 1/4$. For ordered nonnegative bounded potentials, one fixed nonzero nonnegative input and one point measurement suffice for every $0<s<1$.

title: An approximate inner ball condition characterizing $C^{1,α}$ convex bodies
abstract: The main result of this paper uses an approximate inner ball condition to characterize $C^{1,α}$ convex bodies for $0<α\leq 1$. In particular, we show that a convex body $K$ is of class $C^{1,α}$ if and only if there exist constants $C,\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for every $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0$ and for every $x\in\partial K$ there exists $h^\varepsilon(x)$ satisfying $B(h^\varepsilon(x), C\varepsilon^\frac{1-α}{1+α})\subset K$ and $\operatorname{dist}(x,B(h^\varepsilon(x), C\varepsilon^\frac{1-α}{1+α}))\leq\varepsilon.$ We then give a new proof of the regularity of the convex envelope by showing that $\operatorname{conv}(f)\in C^{1,α}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ whenever $f\in C^{1,α}_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $f$ satisfies the coercivity condition $f(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Finally, we use the approximate inner ball characterization of $C^{1,α}$ convex bodies to prove that the Minkowski sum of a $C^{1,α}$ convex body and a nonempty closed convex set is a $C^{1,α}$ convex domain.

title: Computer-assisted proofs of periodic solutions of state-dependent delay equations beyond perturbative regimes
abstract: Rigorous existence results for periodic solutions of state-dependent delay differential equations (SDDEs) are scarce outside perturbative regimes, where the equation is close to an ordinary or constant-delay differential equation. We develop a computer-assisted framework that proves the existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs directly. The numerical approximation is a trigonometric polynomial, and a true periodic solution nearby is obtained by a Newton--Kantorovich argument in the space of $C^1$ periodic functions. The main difficulty lies in the terms in which the solution is evaluated at a time that itself depends on the solution. We obtain rigorous enclosures of their Fourier coefficients by adapting validated discrete Fourier transform techniques for analytic nonlinearities. We apply the framework to three representative examples of increasing complexity: a periodically forced toy model, an autonomous scalar equation with two state-dependent delays, and a threshold-type delay model from operon dynamics in gene regulation. To our knowledge, these are the first computer-assisted proofs of existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs outside perturbative regimes. This opens the way to computer-assisted proofs for SDDEs more broadly. All computer-assisted proofs, including the requisite codes and the approximate objects, are accessible on GitHub at \cite{code_proof}.

title: One-dimensional second-gradient elasticity: pantograph-inspired energies and solitary waves
abstract: We present a self-contained formulation of longitudinal motion in one-dimensional second-gradient continua. Starting from finite-strain kinematics, we then apply the Principle of Virtual Power to identify the governing field equation and contact actions, derive the balance laws, and establish the mechanical-energy identity for hyperelastic materials. Motivated by pantographic microstructures, we study a class of finite-strain energies formulated in terms of normalized strain measures and deformation-dependent strain-gradient moduli. For the associated equation of motion, a traveling-wave first integral yields a turning-point criterion for the existence of solitary waves with positive stretch, exponential decay, and finite mechanical energy, as well as uniqueness at each fixed speed within a prescribed strain interval. For suitable spring energies, a change of strain variable reduces this integral to a polynomial equation, yielding explicit tensile and compressive profiles for Green--Lagrange and Hencky strains under appropriate parameter and kinematic conditions. Under the positivity condition on the quartic potential, the constructed Hencky energy has several physically natural properties: it is nonnegative, admits the natural state as its unique zero and global minimizer, has a positive linearized modulus, penalizes stretch gradients, and diverges under both material collapse and unlimited extension. Furthermore, the stored energy is coercive with respect to the $H^1$ norm of logarithmic strain. Together with mechanical-energy conservation, this yields uniform upper and positive lower bounds on stretch throughout the lifespan of smooth solutions. The theory's accessible mechanical origin, relatively simple mathematical foundation, and diverse solitary waves offer a tractable entry point to studying the rich nonlinear dispersive equations governing higher-gradient elastic continua.

title: Mutation-acyclicity in rank four is decidable but not semialgebraic
abstract: We prove that mutation-acyclicity of quivers on four vertices is decidable. If a four-vertex quiver $Q$ is mutation-acyclic, then some sequence of mutations takes it to an acyclic quiver without any arrow multiplicity exceeding $\operatorname{max}\{\operatorname{ht}(Q),m(Q)\}$, where $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ is the largest arrow multiplicity of $Q$ and $m(Q)$ is the Markov invariant of Fomin and Neville evaluated on the totally proper wiggle class of $Q$. A search within a computable form of this bound decides mutation-acyclicity of four-vertex quivers with $O(h^{24})$ states for input height $h\ge1$. Together with a theorem of Caldero and Keller, it also decides mutation equivalence of two four-vertex quivers up to relabeling whenever one of them is mutation-acyclic. We conjecture that $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ alone suffices as the bound, which would reduce the search to $O(h^{6})$ states, and we verify this for all four-vertex quivers of height at most three. In the other direction, for every $n\ge4$ we construct an affine family of connected $n$-vertex quivers whose nonnegative even members are mutation-acyclic and whose positive odd members are mutation-cyclic. Consequently, unlike in rank three, no fixed finite Boolean combination of polynomial equations and strict polynomial inequalities in the arrow weights (i.e., a semialgebraic criterion) decides mutation-acyclicity of $n$-vertex quivers, even allowing polynomials that are not mutation-invariant. Finally, we correct the criterion for four-vertex quivers of height at most two stated in our earlier paper, and recover its classification counts with short certificates. The calculations in the proof of the height bound are verified by computer for all values of their parameters.

title: Stability of Doubly Indexed Discrete Linear Systems
abstract:
We study the stability of the two-dimensional discrete dynamical system defined by
  \[ x_{i,j} = A x_{i-1,j} + B x_{i,j-1},\]
  where $A, B \in \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$. Although this system, commonly known as the Fornasini-Marchesini model, has been examined for decades, several key stability results have lacked rigorous proofs. This paper establishes precise and self-contained criteria for Lyapunov, asymptotic, and neutral stability under general bounded boundary conditions. In particular, we prove that asymptotic stability is equivalent to the spectral condition $ ρ(z_1 A + z_2 B) < 1 $ for all $ |z_1| \leq 1, |z_2| \leq 1 $. We further analyze the commutative case, derive recurrence relations for anti-diagonal sums, and present new examples and counterexamples illustrating the nuances of stability. The results are complemented by sufficient conditions based on matrix norms, Lyapunov functions, and the joint spectral radius.

title: Delooping levels on Morita context algebras
abstract: We study the behavior of various delooping levels in the setting of Morita context algebras with zero bimodule homomorphisms. Building on the notion of syzygies for modules over such algebras, we establish conditions under which the delooping level (see [6]) of a Morita context algebra is finite, provided that the component algebras also have finite delooping levels. We further extend these results to other invariants, the global delooping level (see [2]) and the derived delooping level (see [8]), showing how their finiteness is preserved in the Morita context. Several examples illustrate both the applicability of our criteria and the necessity of the hypotheses, highlighting cases where the delooping level of the whole algebra can be smaller than that of its components.

title: Computations in weight 3 of higher Bloch groups
abstract: We computationally investigate a weight 3 analogue of the relationship between higher Bloch groups, algebraic K-theory, higher regulators, and special values of Dedekind zeta functions. In particular, for F a number field F, we define the pruned Bloch group B _3(F) and compare the covolume of its regulator lattice with zeta_F(3). We define a quantity kappa_3(F), which is conjecturally an integer, that is expected to be closely related to the order of K_4(O_F).

title: Hankel determinants for the $(n+2)$-shifted $q$-metallic numbers
abstract: Let $Φ_n(q)$ denote the $q$-deformation (in the sense of Morier-Genoud & Ovsienko) of the metallic number $φ_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$. This is a power series with integer coefficients. We prove that the Hankel continued fraction of the $(n+2)$-shifted series $Φ_n^{(n+2)}$ is eventually periodic, and that the corresponding Hankel determinant sequence $Δ^{(n+2)}$ is $2n(n+1)$-periodic if $n$ is even, $2n(n+1)$-antiperiodic if $n$ is odd, and that it takes only the values $-2,-1,0,1,2$. This confirms part of a former conjecture of ours and complements similar results we obtained for all $\ell$-shifts of $Φ_n$ with $0\le\ell\le n+1$. In addition, we formulate a new conjecture of quasi-polynomiality for higher shifts $\ell\ge n+3$. The determinant values arise as telescoping products of the partial numerators of the Hankel continued fraction. Most of the technically involved and lengthy verifications are carried out by a symbolic computation program, whose code is publicly available on GitHub for independent verification.

title: Non-comparable invariant metrics and failure of Gromov hyperbolicity on a real-analytic pseudoconvex domain
abstract:
We study the explicit bounded pseudoconvex domain \[
  Ω=\{(z_1,z_2,w)\in\mathbb C^3:
  |w|^2+|z_1z_2(z_1-z_2)|^2+|z_1|^8+|z_2|^8<1\}. \] Its boundary is real analytic and has finite D'Angelo type everywhere. We prove two assertions about the invariant metrics of this domain. First, $(Ω,k_Ω)$ is not Gromov hyperbolic; in fact arbitrarily fat Kobayashi geodesic triangles occur in every neighborhood of the type-$8$ point $(0,0,1)$. Second, the Carathéodory--Reiffen and Kobayashi--Royden metrics are not uniformly comparable. Along an explicit family of tangential directions the Carathéodory metric tends to zero while the Kobayashi metric has a positive limit. For the corresponding distances there are points $x_j,y_j\to(0,0,1)$ such that $c_Ω(x_j,y_j)\to0$ while $k_Ω(x_j,y_j)\to\infty$. This gives, among bounded real-analytic pseudoconvex domains, an affirmative answer to Problem~7.3.2 of the Several Complex Variables Problem List.

title: Spectral $Γ_2$ inequalities for the $V$-Laplacian with evolving weighted measures
abstract: In this paper, we establish spectral Bakry-Émery $Γ_2$ criteria and their modified counterparts for the $V$-Laplacian on closed Riemannian manifolds equipped with evolving weighted measures. The estimates yield jointly optimized spectral bounds and sharp endpoint constants. When the measures evolve according to the Fokker-Planck equation, these estimates yield monotonicity formulas for the Fisher information associated with Shannon and Tsallis entropies, together with quantitative propagation of Poincaré, logarithmic Sobolev, and nonlinear interpolation inequalities. In the stationary reversible setting, our results specialize to the Witten Laplacian and recover the unweighted Cai-Wang estimates \cite{Cai}.

title: Minimax Rates for Robust Gaussian Mean Estimation Near the Breakdown Point under Constraints
Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions
abstract: High-frequency control problems are often studied through time discretization, but refining the timestep $δ$ increases the discrete horizon $H=T/δ$ and can make standard finite-horizon regret guarantees deteriorate even when the physical horizon $T$ is fixed. We study episodic value-based reinforcement learning for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions. The performance is measured as the cumulative regret over $K$ episodes relative to the optimal policy of the corresponding Euler model. Under stability and regularity conditions on value function gradients, Bellman residual derivatives, and fitted critics, we prove an $\mathcal{O}(\log K)$ regret bound with constants uniform in $δ$. For dynamics with drift linear in unknown parameters and unknown constant diffusion covariance, we verify localized versions of these conditions for a constrained, model-based controlled-diffusion fitted-$Q$ algorithm (CD-FQ) and obtain high-probability $\mathcal{O}(\log K\log\log K)$ regret for fixed and finite $T$, again with constants uniform in $δ$.

title: ODAT-SE: A modular and parallel framework for simulation-based inverse problems
abstract: Open Data Analysis Tool for Science and Engineering (ODAT-SE) is an open-source Python framework for inverse problems that are solved by repeated forward simulations. It succeeds 2DMAT, which was developed for surface-structure analysis with quantum-beam diffraction and has since been applied to other fields. In version 3, the search algorithms were separated from the application-specific solvers, which became independent packages, and the software was renamed; this paper describes the current version 4.0. The framework connects optimization and sampling algorithms to solvers through a common interface for parameter mapping, constraints, and objective evaluation, so that an existing simulation code can be used with any of the algorithms. Relative to the previously published 2DMAT, it provides two-level MPI parallelism, which distributes candidate evaluations over processes and each evaluation over a parallel solver, checkpoint and continuation facilities, random search, global optimizers from SciPy, tensor-train optimization, and a Bayesian workflow that estimates partition-function ratios, model evidence, effective noise levels, and marginal posterior distributions. We validate the Bayesian workflow against closed-form results for a linear regression, benchmark tensor-train optimization on continuous, binary, and mixed-integer problems, and verify the two-level parallelization by the same optimum for all process decompositions. Taking up the positron-diffraction example of the 2DMAT paper, the workflow identifies the correlated structural solutions and an effective noise scale close to the imposed perturbation, while exposing incomplete convergence of symmetry-related mode weights. Solver packages, templates, and a gallery of examples support the use of the framework as a general platform for inverse-problem analysis.

title: The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends
abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.

title: The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian Conjecture
abstract: Let $h\in\C[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ have constant nonzero Hessian determinant, let $h^{*}$ be its formal Legendre transform and $g=\vv{X,\grad h}-h$. The Nambu derivations of $\grad h$ satisfy $δ_i(g)=X_i$ and $δ^α(g)=(\partial^αh^{*})\circ\grad h$. Consequently, in the gradient case the differential Galois criterion of \cite{ACH19}, consisting of $n$ membership conditions, reduces to a single membership condition. Equivalently, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $g\in\C[\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh]$. Moreover, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $δ^α(g)=0$ for $|α|=(°h-1)^{n-1}+2$, and then the coefficients $δ^α(g)(x_0)/α!$ of $h^{*}$ at $\grad h(x_0)$ determine the inverse. If the Hessian determinant of $h$ is merely a nonzero polynomial, then $g$ is still a primitive element of $\C(X)$ over $\C(\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh)$. For the Nambu-tower criterion, doubling a Keller map yields no independent conditions. After an affine change of coordinates putting $\grad h$ in the normal form $X+H$, the formal Legendre transform is the sum of the formal Pascal difference series of $g$, and the termination of this series implies polynomial invertibility. In at most three variables the normal form of every gradient Keller map has strongly nilpotent Jacobian part and is therefore Pascal finite, by a theorem of de Bondt, and an explicit gradient automorphism in four variables has a normal form which is not Pascal finite. The five-variable counterexample of Meng and Yang shows that the properties used here do not imply the Hessian conjecture. The results do not settle the open cases $\JC_2$ and $\HC_4$.

title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

title: Grassmannian Realizations of Classical Pseudo-Riemannian Symmetric Spaces
abstract: We establish a unified fixed-point Grassmannian framework for the classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces from Berger's classification. For a classical group $G=\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(V,b)$, we identify $G$ with the open graph-like locus inside an ordinary or maximal-isotropic Grassmannian $\overline{G}$. Natural involutions of $\overline{G}$ are constructed via classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations. We explicitly describe the full fixed loci of these involutions in terms of classical Grassmannians. The corresponding graph-like fixed loci (or their signature strata) are identified, respectively, with the moduli spaces of classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations; these moduli spaces coincide with classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces. In summary, the 54 classical series are organized into four families: 10 group-type models, 7 classical-form Grassmannians, 20 scalar-structure Grassmannians, and 17 subspace-configuration Grassmannians.

title: Ancestor Lifting of Quasi-Cyclic Additive Codes and Certified Quantum Codes
abstract: Additive codes over $\Ffour$ that are self-orthogonal under the trace inner product correspond to binary quantum stabilizer codes. We study 1-generator $(1,2)$-quasi-cyclic (QC) additive codes and their exact quantum distances. For composite lengths $n=\ell m$, an ancestor-lifting theorem transports dual words of the folded ancestor to the length-$n$ code. A two-layer decomposition for $\ell=2$ and a CRT splitting for odd $\ell$ yield dimension laws and explain equality, escape, and mixed-branch behavior in the certified examples. A palindromic criterion ensures symplectic self-orthogonality, while reversal pairing and a symplectic Gram rank formula describe broader construction families. Exact distances are established by information-set decoding screening, Brouwer--Zimmermann computation on the additive dual, and independent witness verification. We certify twenty-one record-breaking binary quantum codes across twenty entries of Grassl's code table, with twenty-eight certified members in total. Propagation improves thirty-four further entries, and explicit constructions are supplied for three table-tying GV entries marked Code Missing Construction. Six additional candidates are reported only with rigorous upper bounds and heuristic screening evidence. The results connect divisor-lattice structure in additive quasi-cyclic codes with reproducible certification of exact quantum distances.

title: Diameter Bounds and Finiteness of Graphs from Local Intersection Data
abstract:
We extend the Bakry--Émery curvature framework on graphs, broadening its applications and strengthening the resulting diameter bounds. We study diameter bounds and finiteness for amply regular graphs, distance-regular graphs, $(s,c,a,k)$-graphs, and locally strongly regular graphs. In particular, for an amply regular graph with parameters $(v,k,λ,μ)$, we prove that \[{\rm{diam}}(G)\le4+8\log\frac{k}{λ+2}\] when $μ>2$ and $k\ge3λ^2/μ$, improving the previous linear bound $4k/(λ+4)$ to a logarithmic bound.
  We also address several related conjectures. In their monograph \emph{Distance-Regular Graphs}, Brouwer, Cohen, and Neumaier conjectured that every amply regular graph with $μ>1$, except the icosahedron, satisfies ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le2k/(λ+2)$. We confirm this bound when $μ>λ+1$ and give counterexamples to the conjecture with $μ=λ$. For amply regular graphs with $μ\geλ$ and $μ>1$, we obtain ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le 2k/μ+1$. This proves the Qiao--Park--Koolen conjecture.
  In 1983, Terwilliger conjectured that every $(s,c,a,k)$-graph with $c>1$ is finite. We prove this conjecture when $s>2$, $c>2$, and $(s,c)\ne(4,3)$. Moreover, we prove Weetman's finiteness conjecture for locally strongly regular graphs when the local parameter $μ>1$, and disprove his stronger conjecture that every strongly regular graph is an $\mathscr{S}$-graph. We also prove that every graph whose local graphs all have rank 3 is finite, which in particular proves a conjecture of Soicher in 1992.

title: Degree-truncated DP-colouring of $\{K_4,K_{2,t}\}$-minor-free graphs
abstract:
A graph $G$ is degree-truncated DP-$k$-colourable (respectively, degree-truncated $k$-choosable) if it is DP-$f$-colourable (respectively, $f$-choosable), where $f(v)=\min\{k,d_G(v)\}$ for every vertex $v$. Hutchinson proved that every $2$-connected maximal outerplanar graph other than the triangle is degree-truncated $5$-choosable. Lo, Wang, Zhou and Zhu strengthened this result by proving that every $2$-connected $K_{2,4}$-minor-free graph other than cycles and complete graphs is degree-truncated DP-$5$-colourable.
  Outerplanar graphs are precisely the $\{K_4,K_{2,3}\}$-minor-free graphs. We study how the truncation threshold grows when $K_{2,3}$ is replaced by $K_{2,t}$, while $K_4$-minor remains excluded. A bound independent of $t$ is impossible, as shown by the family $\{K_{2,n}| n\ge 2\}$. Let $\mathcal S_t$ be the class of $2$-connected $\{K_4,K_{2,t}\}$-minor-free graphs other than cycles. Writing $χ^{\text{\sout{d}}}_{\mathrm{DP}}(\mathcal S_t)$ for the least truncation threshold valid throughout this class, we prove that, for every integer $t\ge3$, \[ \left\lfloor2\sqrt{2t}\right\rfloor \le χ^{\text{\sout{d}}}_{\mathrm{DP}}(\mathcal S_t) \le \left\lceil4\sqrt{2t}\right\rceil. \]

title: Wasserstein approximation of measures via orthogonal frames: statistical and computational complexities
abstract: Dimension-reduction methods such as PCA identify a subspace capturing most of the variation in the data, but not a distinguished basis within it. Selecting a basis in which the samples are sparsely represented is a recurring task in unsupervised learning, addressed by methods in factor analysis, dictionary learning, and subspace clustering. We pose this task as Wasserstein approximation of the data distribution by measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame, which, in turn, reduces to a nonsmooth optimization problem over the orthogonal group $\mathrm{O}(d)$. We show that, under mild assumptions, both empirical risk minimizers and a locally initialized stochastic gradient method recover the population-optimal frame at the near-parametric rate $\widetilde{O}_d(n^{-1/2})$, where $n$ is the sample size. The main difficulty is that, although the population objective is smooth, the empirical objective is not-this mismatch precludes standard covering arguments. We overcome this issue by replacing Lipschitz continuity of the empirical gradient with a coarsely Lipschitz bound, a tool that may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments support our theoretical findings.

title: Energy equality and renormalization of Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
abstract: We study weak solutions of the incompressible and the compressible Navier--Stokes--Vlasov systems on a bounded domain, where a viscous fluid is coupled to a dispersed particle phase through a drag force; the fluid obeys the no-slip boundary condition and the particles are subject to specular reflection. For solutions with Besov regularity, we show that the Vlasov equation is renormalizable in the sense of DiPerna--Lions, and we give regularity thresholds for the validity of the global energy equality. If the distribution function $f$ belongs to $B_p^{α,\infty}$ in space and velocity with time integrability $p$, and the fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to $B_q^{β,\infty}$ jointly in space and time with integrability $q$, then the energy equality holds provided $α+β>1$ and $β$ exceeds an explicit bound depending on $p$, $q$ and the dimension, under a natural integrability assumption on the pressure; an analogous criterion holds for the compressible system when the density is bounded from above and below. The condition $αp>1$ imposed on $f$ is not merely technical: it is exactly the range in which the macroscopic momentum flux possesses a boundary trace, so that the specular reflection condition passes to the macroscopic energy balance. When the particle phase is absent, our thresholds coincide with the criteria $β>\frac12+\frac1q$ and $β>\frac3q$ obtained by Yu for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations alone. The proofs combine a boundary cutoff argument with commutator estimates based on a scale-localized Besov modulus, together with a boundary-strip analysis.

title: Equivalence between rationality and modular invariance under $C_2$-cofiniteness
abstract: We prove that for a simple and $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, the rationality is equivalent to the modular invariance of the space of complete ordinary one-point trace functions of its irreducible modules. This proves a conjecture given by Dong-Ren in \cite{DongRen}, which is also the inverse theorem of Zhu's modular invariance theorem \cite{Zhu}.

title: Resolvent Components of Completely Normal Elements and the Morgan-Mullen Conjecture
abstract: We study completely normal elements of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, that is, elements that are normal over every intermediate field, through partial Lagrange resolvents. In these coordinates, complete normality splits into independent components, in a way closely related to Hachenberger's decomposition theory. Our main tool is a structure theorem for the components; together with a finite computation, it shows that every component has weight (the sum of the probabilities that its conditions fail) at most $3/4$, uniformly in $n$. Combined with the classical character-sum method, this gives an explicit sufficient criterion for the existence of a primitive completely normal element. We verify the criterion for all $n>q$ except $70$ pairs $(q,n)$, which we settle with explicit elements found by computer. Since the case $n\le q$ is due to Garefalakis and Kapetanakis, this confirms the conjecture of Morgan and Mullen (1996) that every $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ contains a primitive element that is completely normal over $\mathbb{F}_q$. The same estimates give two further results. First, Hachenberger's conjectured lower bound $(q-1)^{n'}q^{(p^a-1)n'}$ for the number of completely normal elements, where $p$ is the characteristic and $n=p^an'$ with $p\nmid n'$, holds for all pairs $(q,n)$; it was known for regular pairs. Second, primitivity and complete normality are asymptotically independent: as $q^n\to\infty$, the number of primitive completely normal elements is $(1+o(1))\,\varphi(q^n-1)/(q^n-1)$ times the number of completely normal elements (for fixed $n$ this was known). Our arguments for $n>q$ and for both further results, including every computer-assisted step, are formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the formalisation takes the case $n\le q$ and an explicit bound of Rosser and Schoenfeld as axioms and relies on Lean's compiler and interpreter for the large computations.

title: Detailed balance and phase transition in Nash equilibria of mean-field Ising game
abstract: We study a finite-state mean-field game with entropic control cost. In the large population limit, we show that its stationary Nash equilibria satisfy the detailed balance condition and their distributions take the Gibbsian form with the value function playing the role of a Hamiltonian. We apply the entropic control cost to a ferromagnetic mean-field Ising game and investigate its stationary and non-stationary Nash equilibria. We find that the stationary Nash equilibria exhibit a second-order phase transition from disordered to ordered equilibria as temperature decreases. A center-manifold reduction yields non-stationary Nash equilibrium near the critical temperature and reveals the critical slowing down in the relaxation toward the stationary Nash equilibrium.

title: On the $d$-invariants of Brieskorn spheres and $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$
abstract: We study the $d$-invariant from Heegaard Floer homology for Brieskorn spheres $Σ(p,q,r)$. Using surgeries on two singular fibers, we establish new relations of the $d$-invariants among various Brieskorn spheres. For $p=2$, we show that $d$ never vanishes if $q/r$ lies in certain intervals on the rational line. Altogether, we completely classify Brieskorn spheres $Σ(2,q,r)$ with $d=0$. The zero set is expressed using submonoids of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ and the Stern--Brocot tree. As an application, we prove that most Brieskorn spheres $Σ(2,q,r)$ do not bound a rational homology $4$-ball.

title: Moment representations for generalized Lehmer polynomials
abstract: We represent normalized generalized Lehmer polynomials as moments of a random variable constructed from two independent negative binomial variables and an independent uniform variable. An integral form of their known exponential generating function yields mixtures of uniform distributions and convergent double series. We recover Eulerian polynomial identities and give a probabilistic interpretation of anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. We also prove moment determinacy, characterize the Stieltjes parameter range, derive Hankel total non-negativity and log-convexity, and identify the boundary distributions.

title: Shape optimization under minimal width and constant width constraints
abstract: In this paper we study shape optimization problems for planar convex sets with prescribed minimal width or constant width. We prove that the Reuleaux triangle minimizes torsional rigidity among sets of constant width. We also show that the first Dirichlet-Laplace eigenvalue is maximized by the equilateral triangle under a minimal width constraint and by the Reuleaux triangle under a constant width constraint. The proofs use subsets consisting of a disk and three straight or circular caps. Reflection arguments reduce the study to equilateral configurations, which contain a polygon or a disk polygon depending on one parameter. The same cap constructions give a common proof of the known area, Cheeger and inner parallel area inequalities, and yield sharp bounds for all positive moments of the distance to the boundary. We also prove sharp inequalities for concentric disk intersections and decreasing radial integrals, and compare interaction energies for kernels close to a positive constant. This includes a nonempty interval of positive Riesz exponents. Finally, we investigate whether inclusion monotonicity and Minkowski concavity suffice to obtain these comparisons for other functionals.

title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
abstract: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.

title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
abstract: The curse of dimensionality associated with solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the value function remains a key obstacle for real-time optimal feedback control of high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems. This is especially severe in aerospace applications such as relaminarizing unsteady turbulent flows and recovering from aerodynamic stall where nonlinear dynamics play a significant role. We introduce Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control (BASOC), a model reduction framework which seeks to find directions in state space along which the value function is most sensitive, and the distribution of states exhibits maximum variance along optimal trajectories. BASOC leverages trajectory optimization and the Pontryagin minimum principle to obtain state and co-state (value function gradient) data along locally optimal trajectories for constructing state and gradient covariance matrices. Balancing these matrices provides an oblique projection for approximating the value function, which can also be used to construct reduced-order models and surrogate feedback control laws. We show that for linear-quadratic optimal control problems, BASOC becomes equivalent to a snapshot method for initial condition balancing of the optimally controlled closed-loop realization. The framework is demonstrated on a nonlinear three-dimensional system where POD and balanced truncation are known to perform poorly, and on the nonlinear complex Ginzburg-Landau equation to demonstrate feasibility for larger-scale systems.

title: Integer points for iterated Weierstrass elliptic functions
abstract: Iterated Weierstrass P functions exhibit relationships between period lattices and the dynamics. We connect the dynamical properties to the occurrence of integer and rational points on associated real elliptic curves. Defining a complex number z to be an integer point if both P(z) and P'(z) are integers, we restrict to P when the lattice is real and its invariants g2 and g3 are integers. We study when an integer point lies in the Fatou set of P and when it lies in the Julia set, and if there is any dynamical significance to this. Applying established results on integer solutions to cubic Diophantine equations to the dynamical properties of iterated elliptic P functions, we show integer points at poles of P lie in the Julia set. Integer points can also occur in the Fatou set of P.

title: Sheaves on polynomials and polynomial sheaves
abstract: We show that several Dold-Kan type equivalences can be understood as a passage from constructible sheaves on symmetric products (i.e. spaces of polynomials) to polynomial sheaves in the sense of Goodwillie-Weiss calculus, by means of a natural analytic expansion functor. This geometric perspective provides access to standard tools from sheaf theory such as the six functor formalism and $t$-structures. For example, the equivalence between filtered objects and coherent chain complexes in a stable $\infty$-category receives a geometric incarnation as Verdier duality between $!$-sheaves and $*$-cosheaves on an $\infty$-dimensional simplex. As a main application, we obtain an intrinsic geometric explanation for the appearance of vanishing cycle data for perverse sheaves in a paracyclic variant of the Dold--Kan correspondence pioneered by Dwyer and Kan, at the same time lifting their equivalence to stable $\infty$-categories.

title: Complete Expanding Interval Maps are Mixing
abstract: We give a new and elementary\footnote{That is: without functional analysis.} proof that certain smooth, complete, expanding maps from the interval to itself are mixing.

title: Gross--Prasad conjecture in geometric Langlands
abstract: We prove part of the global Gross--Prasad conjecture for $G = \mathrm{SO}_{n} \times \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ and $H = \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ in the unramified de Rham geometric Langlands setting proposed by Ben-Zvi--Sakellaridis--Venkatesh.

title: An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem
abstract: Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $σ$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner. A pairing-valued approximate identity yields fullness and nondegeneracy.

title: Design of DoF-Robust MIMO via Generalized Pinching Antennas
abstract: Spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) are fundamental to the performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. However, the use of conventional fixed-location antennas introduces disparities in the users' distances to a common base station, which makes the multi-user channel matrix more susceptible to rank deficiency and, consequently, a loss of spatial DoF. This paper shows that generalized pinching antennas can be used to design a new form of MIMO robust to the loss of spatial DoF. In particular, by deploying pinching antennas in close proximity to the users, the resulting multi-user channel Gram matrix can have a well-conditioned, almost diagonal structure, which reduces its sensitivity to the users' spatial deployment as well as the risk of rank deficiency. Two performance metrics, namely the rank-deficiency probability and the outage probability, are used to evaluate the performance of pinching-antenna-assisted MIMO transmission. The presented analytical and simulation results demonstrate the capability of pinching antennas to preserve spatial DoF and provide ubiquitous connectivity by effectively supporting users at spatially separated locations.

title: Integral Forms of Twisted Quantum Affine Algebras and Quantum Frobenius
abstract: For twisted quantum affine algebras, we compare Lusztig's restricted integral form with the integral form generated by group-like toral elements and divided powers of real Drinfeld current modes. The two forms coincide over $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ outside type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$. In type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$, the smallest ordinary localization over which they coincide is $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][Φ_{4r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n=1$, and $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][Φ_{8r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n\geq2$, where $Φ_k(q)$ are cyclotomic polynomials. In particular, no localization obtained by inverting finitely many nonzero Laurent polynomials suffices in this family.

title: Helly theorems for lattice of flats of a matroid
abstract: A basis of a matroid is adapted to a flat if it contains a basis of the flat. We prove that a family of flats in a rank r matroid has a common adapted basis whenever every subfamily of at most r+1 flats does. The ground set and the family may be infinite; only the rank must be finite. This result, in particular, contains Klyachko's vector space Helly theorem for subspaces. As an application, we obtain a splitting criterion for tropical toric vector bundles on projective spaces. As a secondary application, we derive quadratic bounds for the Helly number for distributive generation in the lattice of flats.

title: A Fast Algorithm for Quaternion Tensor Singular Value Decomposition under the QT-Product with Applications to Color Video Processing
abstract: Based on the complex representation of quaternion matrices, this paper revisits the quaternion tensor singular value decomposition (QT-SVD) under the QT-product and establishes the corresponding $z$-block circulant matrix decomposition. We develop an efficient implementation of the QT-SVD. Numerical experiments show that this implementation is substantially faster than QT-SVD based on the quaternion matrix SVD approach \cite[Theorem~2.3]{AMLzhang2022} while maintaining high numerical accuracy. We further apply the QT-SVD to color video encryption and reconstruction. Experiments on five DAVIS video sequences show that the QT-SVD achieves higher reconstruction quality and shorter decomposition times than the quaternion T-SVD \cite{tsvdarxiv} under the same processing procedure. Both methods exhibit comparable ciphertext statistics and differential sensitivity, while the QT-SVD introduces less additional distortion under the tested input perturbations.

title: On module endomorphisms annihilated by residually square-free polynomials over Artinian local PIRs
abstract: We consider finitely generated free modules and their endomorphisms over an Artinian local PIR, also known as an SPIR. We characterize submodules of such modules by constructing minimal generating sets from given bases. We prove that any endomorphism possessing a square-free annihilating polynomial modulo the maximal ideal admits a principal annihilating ideal, and establish that every free invariant submodule under such an endomorphism has an invariant complement. Moreover, for such endomorphisms, we detail the construction of invariant submodules and compute the number of free invariant submodules when the ring is finite. Furthermore, we introduce canonical matrices associated with these endomorphisms, yielding a complete characterization of matrix similarity via invariant polynomials in this context. Finally, we address the non-derogatory case, obtaining a sharper characterization of submodule invariance.

title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
abstract: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schrödinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a spectrum with finite total gap length and the Parreau-Widom property. We also show that the known examples for which Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity has been shown or suggested to fail in the context of the Deift conjecture are in fact Weyl almost periodic. As a result, an accordingly modified version of the Deift conjecture remains a tantalizing open problem.

title: Exact Generic Exponents of Approximation for the Action of the Integral Special Linear Group on the Torus
abstract:
Given an integer $n\ge 2$ and points $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ lying in the $n$--dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ equipped with its usual metric denoted by $\left\langle\;\cdot\;\right\rangle$, let \[ τ_n(\mathbf x,\mathbf y) =
\sup\left\{ τ\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{there exist infinitely many } H\ge1\text{ for which}\\[1mm] \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-τ} \text{ for some } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z) \end{array} \right\} \] be the Diophantine exponent of asymptotic approximation of $\mathbf{y}$ by the orbit of $\mathbf{x}$ under the action of the integral special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$. Let also \[ \widehatτ_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right) =
\sup\left\{ τ\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{for all but finitely many } H\ge1, \text{ there is } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\\[1mm] \text{such that } \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-τ} \end{array} \right\} \] denote the corresponding exponent of uniform approximation.
  The main result of this paper proves that for almost all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{T}^n$ (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure), $$\widehatτ_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; τ_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; n-1.$$ This is the first result to establish the exact generic approximation exponents for an action of a lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ induced by the standard Euclidean action.

title: Propagation Estimates for the Many-body Boson Star Equation
abstract: We study the many-body boson star equation in the mean-field regime. Under a decay assumption on the solution to the effective one-body equation, we prove a uniform-in-time trace-norm estimate comparing the one-particle reduced density matrix of the many-body state with the projection onto the one-body solution. This establishes uniform-in-time mean-field convergence as the particle number goes to infinity. Furthermore, for the many-body dynamics, we establish both a maximal velocity bound, which can be seen as a Lieb--Robinson-type bound, and a minimal velocity bound. As an application, we recover maximal and minimal velocity bounds for the one-body boson star equation by passing to the mean-field limit.

title: The unknotting problem for surfaces in the 4-sphere
abstract: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a closed, connected, orientable, locally flat PL surface in $S^4$ of genus at least 18 (resp. 19) is TOP (resp. PL) unknotted. We prove analogous results for non-orientable surfaces, and for surfaces in any compact PL 4-manifold. We also show that there is an orientable surface in $S^4$ of genus 18 whose group has unsolvable word problem, and an orientable surface in $S^4$ of genus 40 whose group contains an isomorphic copy of every recursively presented group. Similar results hold for non-orientable surfaces.

title: On the interpolation property of Kupferer's Lubin-Tate regulator maps
abstract: Generalizing both [LZ14] and [ScV26, SaV24] we prove the interpolation property at Artin characters of Kupferer's regulator map [Ku20] over a fixed local field $L$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for $p$ any prime. Since our methods cover the case $p=2,$ we in particular close a gap in the literature even for the (cyclotomic) 2-variable regulator map from [LZ14]. Moreover, we study big (dual) Bloch-Kato exponential maps for unramified towers and we use them to improve Colmez' reciprocity law in the Lubin-Tate setting from [SaV24]. Finally, we compare Kupferer's regulator map with the 2-variable regulator map of Loeffler-Zerbes when $L=\mathbb{Q}_p$.

title: Verifying Control Invariance of H-Polytopes is coNP-Complete
abstract: We prove that verifying whether an H-polytope is control invariant for a discrete-time linear system with polytopic input constraints is \textsc{coNP}-complete. This establishes a fundamental computational complexity barrier for set-theoretic control. As an immediate consequence, the exact computation of maximal control invariant subsets of H-polytopes is \textsc{coNP}-hard. These hardness results hold regardless of whether the input constraint set is given in H- or V-representation.

title: Negative edge correlation in complete bipartite graphs
abstract: We prove strict pairwise negative correlation under both the uniform forest measure and the uniform connected-subgraph measure on the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$ for all $m,n\geq2$. Under the connected-subgraph measure, any two distinct edges of a fixed copy of $K_{2,2}$ remain strictly negatively correlated after conditioning on the subgraph induced by the remaining vertices.

title: Reflection equations and Littlewood identities for spin Hall-Littlewood and $q$-Whittaker functions
abstract:
We describe two-parametric Littlewood identities for inhomogeneous stable spin Hall-Littlewood and inhomogeneous spin $q$-Whittaker symmetric functions. These identities generalize the Littlewood identity found by Warnaar (2006) for the ordinary Hall-Littlewood polynomials. However, instead of Rogers-Szegö coefficients used by Warnaar, coefficients in our identities are given by products of Al-Salam-Chihara polynomials.
  Our proof relies on integrable lattice models. A key step includes three new solutions to the reflection and boundary equations for the fully fused six-vertex model. To find these solutions we use isomorphisms between tensor products of evaluation $U_q(L\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-modules, as well as covectors stable under a $q$-Onsager coideal subalgebra.

title: Young's lattice, invariant ideals, and weak identities
abstract: For a $d$-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field of characteristic zero, we show that $GL(V)$-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra of the free two-step nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_2(V)$ are in natural correspondence with filters in Young's lattice of integer partitions with at most $d$ rows. The same classification holds for $GL(V)$-stable Poisson ideals of $S(V\oplusΛ^2(V))$ with its natural Poisson bracket. As applications, we determine all weak polynomial identities of the $n$-th Weyl algebra relative to its standard generating subspace and of the universal enveloping algebra of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra relative to the Lie algebra itself.

title: Non-degeneracy of Hopf triplets
abstract: We study the relationship between semisimplicity and non-degeneracy for finite-dimensional Hopf triplets over a field of characteristic zero. The non-degeneracy condition appears in the construction of \(4\)-manifold invariants from Hopf triplets, and it was not known whether non-semisimple examples satisfying this condition exist. We prove that a Hopf triplet is non-degenerate if and only if it is semisimple.

title: Square-root logarithmic bounds for the arithmetic complexity of factorial multiples
abstract: Assume that the Riemann zeta function has no zeros in $\Re(s)>1-δ$, $s\neq1$, for some fixed $0<δ\leq1/2$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, a positive multiple $m_k k!$ has arithmetic complexity $τ(m_k k!)\leq\exp(C\sqrt{\log k\log\log k})$, where $C$ depends only on $δ$. We first establish a smooth-number asymptotic at every sufficiently large center $x$ in intervals of length at least $x^{3/4}$. Combining this estimate with an established genus-two construction yields the arithmetic bound without Cheng's conjecture on smooth numbers in elliptic Hasse intervals. The bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.

title: Hybridizing 0/1 Knapsack and Priority-Aware TSP for Vehicle Routing: an Applied Variant of the TSP with Profits
abstract: Distribution logistics with capacity constraints and service priorities can be modeled as a variant of the \emph{TSP with Profits} (TSPP), in which not all customers need to be visited and the selection of which customers to serve is part of the problem. This paper proposes an applied variant with two adaptations: (i) a 0/1 Knapsack objective function weighted by client priority squared ($v_i \cdot p_i^2$), and (ii) a priority bias in the Nearest Neighbor heuristic for the TSP, parameterized by $α$. The approach is evaluated on a scenario with 14 customers and a 1,100~kg capacity, complemented by a comparative experimental protocol against the classical greedy heuristic ($v_i/w_i$ ordering) and an integer programming solver. Results on the base scenario show 9 customers served, 96.4\% capacity utilization, and R\$~18,392.60 revenue, with all 5 excluded customers being low-priority. A sensitivity analysis of the priority exponent justifies the quadratic choice. The limitations of the hierarchical decomposition are explicitly discussed.

title: Failure of the congruence Hasse principle for commutators in orientable surface groups
abstract: Ghosh, Meiri and Sarnak showed that the commutator equation over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfies a profinite local to global principle, and that for a prime $\ell\equiv\pm1$ mod $5$ it fails for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell])$ with a reciprocity obstruction. We extend the failure to surface groups. For the genus-$2$ surface group $Γ_2$ we construct an explicit representation $ρ:Γ_2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, where $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1}{10}]$, whose quotients modulo the maximal ideals are the full groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ except in residue characteristic $3$, where the quotient has order $24$. For every $k\ge2$ the word $[a_1,b_1]^k$ is not a commutator in $Γ_2$, while its image is a commutator in every one of these quotients. The same holds for every surface group $Γ_g$ with $g\ge2$.

title: Archimedean zeta integrals on $ {\rm SO}_{2n} \times {\rm GL}_n$ and $ {\rm Sp}_{2n} \times {\rm GL}_n $
abstract: We evaluate the archimedean Rankin-Selberg zeta integrals associated with spherical principal series representations of ${\rm SO}_{2n}(\mathbf R) \times {\rm GL}_n(\mathbf R) $ and $ {\rm Sp}_{2n}(\mathbf R) \times {\rm GL}_n(\mathbf R) $, where $ {\rm SO}_{2n} $ is split and $n\ge2$. We obtain explicit formulas expressing these integrals as quotients of products of gamma functions. Our approach uses Mellin-Barnes representations of spherical Whittaker functions, together with new integral identities for their Mellin transforms and transformations of Barnes integrals. In the even orthogonal case, we establish a recurrence in the rank and evaluate the integral by induction. The symplectic case then follows from an explicit identity relating the two families of zeta integrals.

title: Global Well-posedness and Asymptotic Extinction for Keller-Segel Systems with Superlinear Noise
abstract: It is well known that solutions to deterministic Keller--Segel chemotaxis systems can blow up in finite time under certain conditions. To investigate whether noise can prevent such blow-up, we study parabolic--elliptic and fully parabolic Keller--Segel systems on smooth bounded domains with pointwise superlinear multiplicative Itô noise $σ_0u^r\,\mathrm dW_t$, where $W$ is a real Brownian motion. Our results show that superlinear multiplicative noise can prevent finite-time blow-up in Keller--Segel systems. For $r>3/2$, we prove global existence and pathwise uniqueness of nonnegative mild solutions in arbitrary spatial dimension, for every $σ_0>0$. At $r=3/2$, both systems are globally well-posed in two dimensions for every positive noise intensity; in arbitrary dimension, the parabolic--elliptic system is global under $σ_0^2\ge2χ$. For $r>3/2$ in the fully parabolic case, the proof combines a logarithmic estimate for the time derivative of the chemical signal with comparison of the local solution to the solution of a scalar stochastic differential equation. The two-dimensional case follows from mass quadratic variation, deterministic maximal regularity, and localized energy estimates. We also establish almost-sure $L^1$ extinction and algebraic decay of fractional mass moments.

title: Log-concavity of longest increasing subsequence
abstract: We prove a conjecture proposed by Chen that, for every fixed $n$, the sequence $(a_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave, where $a_{n,k}$ counts permutations of $[n]$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$.

title: Large data global strong solutions to the quantum Navier-Stokes equations with degenerate viscosity
abstract: This work is devoted to study the Cauchy problem for the quantum Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb R^N$, $N=2,3$, with density dependent viscosities $μ(ρ)=ρ,λ(ρ)=0$, quantum capillarity $κ(ρ)=1/ρ$, which was derived by Dunn and Serrin (see Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 88(2):95-133, 1985) as a phase transition model. For arbitrarily large initial data satisfying suitable regularity and decay assumptions, with density positive at every finite point and vanishing at infinity, we prove the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without symmetry assumptions. The admissible pressure range is $γ\ge 1$ in two dimensions and $1\leγ< 8/3$ in three dimensions. On every finite time interval, the density remains pointwise comparable to its initial profile, and both the effective velocity and the logarithmic density gradient remain bounded. The central estimates require no uniform positive lower bound for the density. When $γ>1$, a suitable combination of the density and effective velocity equations allows the maximum principle to yield an $L^\infty$ bound for the effective velocity using only an upper bound for the density. We then introduce the relative density with respect to a fixed profile determined by the initial data. In the isothermal case $γ=1$, we combine estimates for this relative density with a scalar inequality involving the effective velocity and the logarithmic density to close the coupled estimates and obtain the effective velocity bound. Combining the relative-density bounds with weighted gradient estimates and localized De Giorgi iteration, we control the logarithmic density gradient and close the higher-order estimates.

title: Effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate distribution for Abelian varieties with applications
abstract: We establish a uniform effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimate for abelian varieties, conditional on the Mumford-Tate conjecture and the standard analytic conjectures for L-functions attached to the irreducible representations of the Chebotarev-Sato-Tate group. The proof uses spectral majorants and minorants of indicator functions. For regions whose boundaries have finite upper (d-1)-dimensional Minkowski content, the resulting exponent improves that in Bucur et al. (Theorem 1.1, 2024) whenever the Sato-Tate group has rank greater than one. We establish uniform estimates for regions and finite Galois extensions that vary with the counting parameter, and for prime-dependent regions satisfying an explicit variation condition. As an application, we obtain a conditional upper bound for the number of primes at which a weight-two newform with a quadratic coefficient field has a rational Fourier coefficient. We also formulate a discrepancy conjecture, motivated by a probabilistic model, that implies the asymptotic predicted by Murty (Conjecture 3.4, 1999).

title: Linear Programming Upper Bounds for the Coil-in-the-Box Problem
abstract: Let $S_n$ denote the maximum length of a coil in the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$, i.e., a simple cycle whose induced subgraph has no additional chords. We combine classical square-counting identities and structural properties of maximum coils with new valid combinatorial inequalities into a parameterized linear program whose optimal value provides an upper bound for $S_n$. For $n\ge13$, we construct two analytic dual feasible solutions. Their objective values yield upper bounds on $S_n$, and the smaller value is the exact optimum of the parameterized LP. One dual solution results in the bound \[ S_n\le 2^{n-1} \frac{8n(n-1)(5n-14)} {40n^3-131n^2+4n+136-(5n-14)\lfloor3n/4\rfloor}, \] which improves upon the upper bounds in Lukito, Lukito-van Zanten, and Zémor for $13\le n\le19853$. The second yields the upper bound \[ S_n\le 2^{n-1}\left( 1-\frac1{30\sqrt{3n}}+O(n^{-1}) \right), \] improving upon the asymptotic upper bound of Zémor. Taken together, the two bounds improve upon the upper bounds for $S_n$ in Lukito, Lukito-van Zanten, and Zémor for every $n\ge13$.

title: The inverse Monge--Ampère flow on klt Fano varieties
abstract: We establish the long time existence of the inverse Monge--Ampère flow on a klt $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety $X$. We further prove that $X$ admits a Kähler--Einstein metric if and only if the flow converges in $L^1$.

title: Tropical spin Hurwitz numbers
abstract: We introduce a tropical framework for the study of spin Hurwitz numbers and their completed cycles analogues. We use degeneration techniques to obtain an interpretation of spin Hurwitz numbers via tropical covers. We employ the tropical methods to obtain new closed formulae for spin Hurwitz numbers in special cases. Moreover, we employ Fock space techniques to tropicalise completed cycles spin Hurwitz numbers. Using this, we prove that spin Hurwitz numbers admit a piecewise polynomial structure akin to their classical counterparts. We also derive wall--crossing formulae.

title: Asynchronous Parallel Computation of Lagrangian Bounds for Mixed-Integer Stochastic Programs by Frank-Wolfe Methods within Projective Hedging
abstract: We describe an asynchronous parallel method to calculate Lagrangian bounds for mixed-integer stochastic programming problems. As in some prior work, we use a fully corrective Frank-Wolfe method on subproblems within a decomposition method, eventually optimizing subproblems for individual scenarios over the convex hulls of their integer-feasible vertices. However, instead of using progressive hedging as our decomposition algorithm, we employ an asynchronous projective hedging method. Like our earlier work on projective hedging, our algorithm need only solve a subset of the scenario subproblems at each iteration. Here, we further exploit the capabilities of projective hedging to create a parallel implementation capable of fully asynchronous operation. As we demonstrate empirically, this capability can lead to significant efficiency improvements when the subproblems are solved by Frank-Wolfe and have highly variable solve times.

title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
abstract: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph is obtained from its iterated basin and hill boundaries. The unweighted counts of extrema at these levels need not satisfy Morse inequalities. We assign multiplicities by the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain the vertices with nonzero local homology. The resulting graph preserves both boundary hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its descending and ascending Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We also construct a Morse chain complex and compute the local groups in several examples. Finally, we consider homology on the original Maxwell graph and prove analogous inequalities for path homology using relative local groups.

title: A convexity theorem for proper Dupin hypersurfaces in spheres
abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a (compact, connected, and embedded) proper Dupin hypersurface in a sphere then, viewing $M$ as a submanifold of the ambient Euclidean space, its orthogonal projection to the normal space at any point is convex. This is a generalization of the convexity theorem of Terng for isoparametric submanifolds in Euclidean spaces.

title: On the Fundamental Limits of Bistatic ISAC Over Vector Channels
abstract: This paper studies the fundamental limits of bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems over vector channels. We first consider a class of parallel channels in which, on each component channel, the channel from the transmitter (Tx) to the communication receiver (Rx) is degraded with respect to the channel from the Tx to the sensing Rx, or vice versa, where the direction of degradation may vary across component channels. For this class of channels, we establish matching achievability and converse results, which yield a single-letter characterization of the capacity-distortion function $C(D)$. For parallel Gaussian channels with additive Gaussian states, the evaluation of the capacity-distortion-power function $C(D,P)$ under the squared error distortion measure reduces to a joint power and distortion allocation problem across the component channels. We then extend the analysis to general vector channels and derive single-letter lower and upper bounds on $C(D)$. In particular, for vector Gaussian channels with additive Gaussian states, we prove the optimality of Gaussian superposition coding without requiring a global degradation order between the communication and sensing channels, by combining the channel enhancement technique with a matrix extremal inequality based on Fisher information. This leads to an exact characterization of $C(D,P)$.

title: Hidden Convexity in Multi-Retailer Cold-Chain Allocation: A Cholesky-Spectral Second-Order Cone Programming Approach
abstract:
Several dairy retailers share a refrigerated cold-chain network, each allocating products across heat-sensitivity subgroups to maximize quadratic-fractional efficiency (DEA style). This formulation measures spoilage risk per unit of logistics cost, separating technical from scale efficiency. The single-agent problem is a non-convex fractional QCQP, while the multi-retailer game forms a generalized Nash equilibrium problem (GNEP) with a shared risk-budget constraint, which is generally NP-hard.
  Governed by the Arrhenius spoilage law, the thermal-risk covariance inherits a rank-one-plus-diagonal structure that unlocks hidden convexity. The authors propose the HSDI (Hidden SOCP Dinkelbach Iteration) algorithm via a joint Cholesky-spectral transform.
  Key contributions include:
  1. Establishing simultaneous diagonalization of without requiring matrix commutativity.
  2. Deriving an explicit sufficient condition for exact second-order cone programming (SOCP) relaxation, alongside a closed-form suboptimality bound for inexact regimes.
  3. Proving global convergence: the outer Dinkelbach loop converges Q-superlinearly (exact) or R-linearly (inexact), and the coupled variational-equilibrium (VE) iteration converges R-linearly under strong monotonicity, achieving an overall complexity while ensuring Lipschitz stability of the primal-dual pair.
  Calibrated on Vietnam and US dairy markets, HSDI matches the objective value of multi-start non-linear baselines without random restarts, yielding global optima under exactness. HSDI exhibits an empirical scaling exponent of 0.93 (versus 1.30 for SLSQP), offering a certified polynomial-time framework and a stable shadow price for prioritizing cold-chain investments.

title: Thermodynamic characterization of message-passing: Framework and initial study
abstract: We study the thermodynamic efficiency of message-passing decoders using the mismatch cost framework. This framework quantifies the excess entropy generated when a system operates away from the thermodynamically optimal initial distribution. It provides a computable lower bound on irrecoverable energy loss. The decoder is modeled as a main decoding program with local message updates implemented as subroutines. Memory is treated as an external copying subsystem whose thermodynamic cost is excluded. Studying the $[7,4]$ Hamming code transmitted over a binary erasure channel, we show how the channel-induced initialization statistics and the step-wise evolution of the algorithmic state distribution during decoding determine the total mismatch cost. We further show that different thermodynamically optimal state distributions, representing different underlying physical implementations of the decoder, can produce different thermodynamic costs for identical decoding dynamics. Conditioning the input distribution on correctable and non-correctable erasure patterns further reveals distinct thermodynamic signatures. These results demonstrate that thermodynamic cost is jointly governed by decoding dynamics, input statistics, and hardware characteristics. This points to opportunities for thermodynamically-informed decoder design to realize energy-efficient physical implementations.

title: Risk measures for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox-BESQ process
abstract: This paper introduces a model for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with stochastic intensity given by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. This MGF can also be obtained at two (or more) dates, thereby allowing an analysis of the time evolution of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox--BESQ process. The availability of these explicit MGFs enables the development of risk measures for these variables, such as the joint moments of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval, conditional on one of these variables exceeding a critical threshold. These risk measures can be determined at one or two dates. They rely essentially on the explicit form of the MGF of the state variables and on Fourier representations of the risk measures. Numerical experiments demonstrate the practical implementation of the proposed methodology and highlight the relevance of the theoretical results.

title: Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator
abstract: Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

title: New upper bounds for average kissing numbers
abstract: A packing of balls in Euclidean space is a set of balls with non-overlapping interiors.
