abstract: We consider positive solutions of \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -Δu=pλh(x)u^{p-1}\mathrm{e}^{u^p}&\text{in }Ω,\\ u>0&\text{in }Ω,\\ u=0&\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p\in[1,2]$, $λ>0$, $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded simply connected domain and $h\in C^2(\overlineΩ)$ is positive on $\overlineΩ$. The cases $p=1$ and $p=2$ correspond to the Liouville and Moser-Trudinger equations, respectively. We prove that the normalized parameter \begin{equation*} β=\frac{λp^2}{2}\left(\int_Ωh(\mathrm{e}^{u^p}-1)\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2-p}{p}}\left(\int_Ωhu^p\mathrm{e}^{u^p}\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2(p-1)}{p}} \end{equation*} is bounded by a constant depending only on $Ω$ and $h$, uniformly over all $p\in[1,2]$, $λ>0$ and positive solutions. At $p=2$, this excludes positive constrained critical points of the weighted Moser-Trudinger functional at sufficiently large Dirichlet energies. For $p=2$ and $h\equiv1$, we further prove that the energy converges uniformly to $4π$ as $λ\to0$ when $Ω$ is convex. We also develop a boundary exclusion argument for positive weights that rules out boundary blow-up for $1<p<2$ without a priori energy bound.

title: The existence of the compatible lattice order on the complex field $\mathbb{C}$
abstract: In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to the open question posed by G.Birkhoff and R.S.Pierce in 1956 concerning the existence of a compatible lattice order on the complex field $\mathbb{C}$. Using valuation rings theory, basis extension in infinite-dimensional vector spaces and extension of field embeddings to algebraic extensions, we obtain that for every real $t>1$ transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}$, the compatible lattice order can be chosen such that $0\prec1$, $0\vee i=t$, and $1\wedge t=0$. Consequently, $\mathbb{C}$ admits at least $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct compatible lattice orders, each extending the usual order on $\mathbb{Q}$.

title: On additive bases of finite abelian groups
abstract:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, and let $c_0(G)$ be the least integer $t$ such that every regular sequence over $G$ of length at least $t$ is an additive basis. Additive bases have been extensively studied in additive combinatorics, and the exact value of $c_0(G)$ has been determined for many groups of rank at least three and some groups of rank two (in which case groups of the form $C_p\oplus C_{pn}$ turn out to be exceptional). In this paper, we continue the study of $c_0(G)$ and obtain the following results.
  (1) Together with known results, we prove that $c_0(G)=|G|/p+p-2$ for all abelian groups $G$ with $\text{rank}(G)\geq 3$.
  (2) For distinct odd primes $p<q$, we determine \[ c_0(C_p\oplus C_{pq})=pq+2p-3,\qquad c_0(C_q\oplus C_{pq})=q^2+p-2. \]
  (3) Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $2\leq a\leq b$, and let $n$ be a positive integer with no prime divisor smaller than $p$. Then \[ c_0(C_{p^a}\oplus C_{p^bn})=p^{a+b-1}n+p-2. \]
  (4) For every odd integer $n\geq 3$, we prove \[ c_0(C_3\oplus C_{3n})=3n+3. \]
  Therefore, $c_0(G)$ is determined except possibly for groups of the form $C_p\oplus C_{pn}$ with $p\geq 5$.

title: Fractal transference principle for conformal iterated function systems
abstract: We establish a complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle connecting density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions. Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemerédi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.

title: Operator Barron Regularity for Elliptic Equations and Application to Neural Operator Approximation
abstract: We develop a spectral Barron regularity framework for nonlinear operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces. Using Hilbert-valued Fourier representations of finite-dimensional input truncations, we establish bounds that are uniform in the input truncation dimension and prove arbitrary-order Barron regularity for a class of elliptic solution operators. Second, we use this operator Barron regularity to derive approximation error bounds for an FNO-type neural operator, with explicit dependence on the input truncation dimension, output reconstruction dimension, and network width. For a fixed input truncation dimension, optimizing the neural approximation bound over the Barron regularity order yields stretched-exponential decay of the approximation error in the network width. We also show some numerical experiments to support the predicted rate.

title: Global well-posedness and scattering of energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on high-dimensional hyperbolic spaces
Three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations
abstract: We show that if a three-manifold $M$ admits a veering triangulation, then the dual spine of every essential triangulation of $M$ can be smoothed to a branched surface. We use this criterion to identify a large collection of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations. We then use the same criterion to construct the first infinite family of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds without veering triangulations.

title: Resolving a Problem of Lv and Koolen on the Smallest Eigenvalue of Distance-Regular Graphs
abstract: Let $Γ$ be a distance-regular graph with valency $k$, diameter $D\ge3$, and eigenvalues $k=θ_0>θ_1>\cdots>θ_D$. Put $b\coloneqq b_1/(θ_1+1)$, and let $1=u_0>u_1>\cdots>u_D$ be the standard sequence associated with $θ_1$. Lv and Koolen asked whether the negative of the smallest eigenvalue of a distance-regular graph can be bounded above in terms of its diameter $D$ and the parameter $b$ alone. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively by proving that $-θ_D\le\prod_{i=2}^D(1-u_i)/(u_1-u_i) <(b+1)^{D-1}$. Equality in the product bound holds if and only if $Γ$ is $Q$-polynomial with respect to the primitive idempotent corresponding to $θ_1$. For every integer $D\ge4$, we further establish the explicit bound $-θ_D\le b^{D-1}+b^{D-2} +\frac{27}{2}(D-2)b^{D-3}$ whenever $b\ge\max\{8,\sqrt{12(D-2)}\}$. Both leading coefficients are best possible for each fixed $D\ge4$. The proof uses a spectral product theorem of Micchelli and Willoughby applied to Schur multiplication in the Bose--Mesner algebra.

title: Quantitative Rigidity of Ricci Nonnegative Manifolds via the Regular Green Constant
abstract: For a Ricci non-negative non-parabolic manifold $(M^{n\ge3},g)$, assuming the minimal normalized Green function admits the asymptotic expansion $G=r^{2-n}+H_p+O_1(r)$, we prove the scaling invariant defect $H_pR^{n-2}$ controls the geometry of the geodesic ball quantitatively, $\frac{1}{R}d_{GH}(B_p(R),B_0^{\mathbb{R}^n}(R))\le C_n \left(H_p R^{n-2}\right)^{\frac{1}{88(n+1)(4n+1)}}$.

title: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions
abstract: How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? Over complex parameters, the admissible equations of a finite loopless multigraph form an algebraic family whose generic degree we determine: it is a graph state sum over edge sets without vertices of degree one, each vertex of positive degree contributing one less than its degree. We give two geometric realizations of this state sum. The first is the total Betti number of a universal edge-incidence ring constructed without parameters. Its full graded Betti table is the state sum, its Tor algebra is natural for noncontracting graph maps, the alternating numerator recovers the graph polynomial of Watanabe and Fukumizu, and an Artin reduction by a regular sequence realizes the one-variable specialization, corrected for tree components. The second lies in the actual family: at the strong-field boundary each state factor is a ramification index, and at sufficiently strong field the state charts exhaust the admissible complex fiber. For fixed nonzero real couplings, every Eulerian message-sign sector contains a real fixed point at every external field, and strong fields attain this lower bound: one admissible real fixed point per element of the binary cycle space and one positive fixed point. For graphs of maximum degree at most three, this minimum equals the number of minimal module generators of the edge-incidence ring. One state decomposition connects the complex degree, graded syzygies, and an attained minimum real count. The degree, selected ring and resolution statements, and the real counts are formalized in Lean 4.

title: Maximal geometric quotients of flag varieties
abstract: We introduce the notion of maximal geometric quotient, namely a geometric quotient of a polarized pair under a torus action which has a birational contraction to any other GIT quotient. For the action of the maximal torus on a complete flag variety, we show that a maximal geometric quotient exists and it is a Mori dream space, and its Cox ring is isomorphic to the Cox ring of the flag variety. We discuss birational properties of the maximal geometric quotients, their relations with the Chow quotients and explain how to construct them for maximal torus actions on flag varieties.

title: On the Minimum Speed for a Fire Blocking Problem
abstract: We consider a dynamic blocking problem: a fire, starting on a bounded open set $R_0\subset\mathbb R^2$, propagates in the plane with unit speed in all directions. To block it, a barrier can be constructed in real time, at speed $λ>0$. A long standing conjecture by the first author states that the fire can be entirely surrounded by the barrier, in finite time, if and only if $λ>2$. The present paper improves on earlier lower bounds. Namely, if $λ\leq Λ=1.62621170228\ldots $ we show that the fire cannot be blocked. We also prove that, if $λ\leq 2$, the fire cannot be blocked by constructing a barrier which is a simple closed curve. More precisely, if the barrier does not contain purely delaying arcs, i.e.~arcs which are eventually surrounded by the fire on both sides, then for $λ<2$ the region burned by the fire at time $t>0$ has area $A(t)>(2-λ)t^2/4$.

title: The sharp exponent for the Banach--Mazur distance to the cube
abstract: Let $R_\infty(n)$ be the maximal Banach--Mazur distance from an $n$-dimensional real normed space to $\ell_\infty^n$. We prove that $R_\infty(n)\ge cn^{2/3}(\log(2n))^{-10}$. Together with the upper bound of Friedland, Naor, and Youssef, this gives $R_\infty(n) = n^{2/3+o(1)}$. The examples are polars of symmetric Gaussian polytopes with $2n$ generators, and the lower bound holds with exponentially high probability. A joint minimization over coefficient representations and positive weights yields an exact second-variation identity and sparse coefficients. A Gaussian projection argument controls all low-rank completions of the recorded matrix. An adaptive choice of exceptional generators then reduces the remaining case to a fixed-shift Gaussian small-ball estimate over two finite nets.

title: On finite covers of projective spaces, generic outside of codimension three
abstract: In the article, we generalize to an arbitrary dimension results obtained by the author and S.Yu. Nemirovski that related to Chisini's conjecture claimed that if $B$ is the discriminant of two generic covers $f_i:X_i\to \mathbb P^2$, $i=1,2$, and $\max (°f_1,°f_2) \geq 5$, then $f_1$ and $f_2$ are equivalent covers.

title: Large deviations from a stable steady state for damped dispersive PDEs with vanishing random kicks
abstract: We study the behaviour of stationary measures for a class of dispersive PDEs damped by a linear zero-order term and perturbed by a small kick noise. Under some natural assumptions on the law of the noise, we prove that any family of stationary measures satisfies the large deviation principle in the vanishing noise limit. The result highlights the role of nonlinear smoothing and applies to the nonlinear Schrödinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations, and to a variety of random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.

title: Laws of the iterated logarithm for the range of once-reinforced random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$
From amplituhedra to flagtopes
abstract: The amplituhedron was introduced by Arkani-Hamed and Trnka (2014) to geometrically encode scattering amplitudes in high-energy physics. It can be viewed as the generalization of a cyclic polytope into the Grassmannian, and is defined to be the projection of the totally nonnegative part of one Grassmannian with respect to a totally negative element of a second Grassmannian. We construct a Lie-theoretic generalization of amplituhedra called 'flag amplituhedra', by replacing the pair of Grassmannians in the definition with an arbitrary pair of partial flag varieties for a reductive group $G$. We study in detail an example of a flag amplituhedron which is not a Grassmannian amplituhedron; it is a curved hexagon in $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^1$.

title: Persistent Hubs and Sharp Asymptotics in Eigenvector Preferential Attachment Trees
abstract: We prove sharp almost-sure asymptotics for eigenvector preferential attachment trees in which each attachment uses eigenvector centrality with probability $α\in(0,1]$ and uniform selection with probability $1-α$. A unique persistent hub eventually has the maximum degree, which is asymptotic to $γ^2t^{2/3}$, where $γ=(9α/10)^{1/3}$. The Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue is asymptotic to $γt^{1/3}$, and the second-largest degree is asymptotic to $2γt^{1/3}$. The hub and its neighbors each carry asymptotically half of the squared Perron mass. We also identify the centrality profile by degree and an explicit mixture of geometric laws for the degree of a uniformly sampled vertex. A limiting distance profile quantifies the dandelion geometry, and vertices beyond the hub's neighbors have maximum degree of order at most $\log t$.

title: High-dimensional critical percolation and critical Branching random walks are intersection equivalent
abstract: We prove that on $\mathbb Z^d$, with $d>6$, and under the usual assumption that the two-point function and the Green's function are of the same order, the probabilities to hit any finite set for a critical Branching random walk starting from the origin and the critical percolation cluster of the origin are within a positive multiplicative constant one from each other, as long as the set is sufficiently far away from the origin comparatively to its diameter. The proof relies on the introduction of a truncated equilibrium measure in percolation and the derivation of an approximate last passage formula.

title: New inhomogeneous Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with large symmetry group
abstract: We study compact non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds whose connected full group of holomorphic isometries acts with cohomogeneity one. We prove that the Lie algebra of this group is isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ or $\mathbb{R}^2\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$, unless the Bismut connection is flat. We then focus on the first case, where we determine the possible singular isotropy algebras and reduce the Bismut Hermitian-Einstein condition to a system of ordinary differential equations. We obtain explicit solutions satisfying suitable smoothness conditions, that yield families of compact and complete non-compact non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with non-constant scalar curvature and non-zero Bismut curvature, including examples on $S^3\times S^3$ and $S^3\times S^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$, respectively. We also investigate the topology of the compact examples and determine the asymptotic scalar curvature of the non-compact ones. Moreover, we prove the existence of a smooth deformation of a Bismut-flat Samelson structure on $S^3\times S^3$ through non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein structures that are not Bismut-flat. The regularity of the constructed compact examples is also investigated.

title: A Two-Stage Optimization Framework for Real-World Large-Scale University Course Timetabling Based on Orthogonalized Hierarchical Modeling and Conflict-Driven ALNS Repair
abstract: University course timetabling is a large-scale combinatorial optimization problem involving strongly coupled temporal and resource constraints. This paper proposes a two-stage optimization framework for real-world large-scale university course timetabling, integrating orthogonalized hierarchical modeling with conflict-driven adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) repair. The first stage performs global course-level optimization, while the second identifies residual conflicts through a conflict graph and localizes them into connected conflict regions. The Course--Occurrence--Session representation provides the structural basis for multi-granularity repair, which employs Cluster-, Course-, Occurrence-, and Session-level destroy operators within the ALNS framework, followed by fine-grained greedy repair. The framework is evaluated on a real-world university timetabling instance involving 3,073 course groups, 8,015 scheduling events, 998 student classes, and 1,511 instructors. Ablation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of hierarchical repair granularity and adaptive operator selection. Across ten independent runs, the ALNS + Greedy framework achieves a mean residual conflict count of 18.50, compared with 172 for deterministic Greedy-only repair under the same initial scheduling conditions, representing an 89.24\% reduction. These results support the effectiveness of the proposed conflict-driven hierarchical repair framework for large-scale university course timetabling.

title: Global Well-Posedness and Large Time Asymptotic Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Compressible Viscous Non-Resistive MHD Equations with Vacuum
abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem to the compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system in $\mathbb{R}^3$, in which the velocity is planar while the magnetic field is vertical. For regular initial data with small energy but possibly large oscillations, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solution with vacuum. In addition, the large-time behavior of the solution is investigated. A key ingredient is an application of the Bourgain--Brezis divergence estimate to handle the total pressure $ρ^γ+m^2$ for any adiabatic index $γ>1$. This enables us to control both components of the total pressure, $ρ^γ$ and $m^2$, by a single estimate that remains valid in the presence of vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, our result is the first one on global solvability to the compressible, viscous, non-resistive MHD system in the special 2$\frac12$-dimensional whole space allowing vacuum.

title: Relative derived delooping levels and torsion intervals
abstract: Let $U$ be a support $τ$-tilting module over a finite dimensional algebra $A$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq \text{Fac}U$ be any torsion class. The heart $\mathcal H=\text{Fac} U\cap \mathcal{V}^\perp$ inherits the exact structure from mod$A$ and admits an Ext-progenerator $P$. Let $B=\text{End}_A(P)$. We define the relative derived delooping level on the exact heart $\mathcal H$ and compare it with the relative delooping level on $\mathcal {H}$ and the derived delooping level of $B$. We show that $\text{Findim} B^{op}$ is bounded by the relative derived delooping level on the $\mathcal H$. For a wide heart, the relative derived delooping level on the heart equals the derived delooping level of $B$. We obtain explicit bounds from representation-finite relative syzygy strata and characterize global first-order finiteness using an Ext-injective cogenerator.

title: On $π$-nilpotencies of finite skew braces
abstract: Let $π$ be a set of primes. We extend the theory of left and right $π$-nilpotency in skew braces beyond the nilpotent type setting, and introduce the study of central $π$-nilpotency for finite skew braces. We investigate the relationships between these three notions, and a characterisation of central $π$-nilpotency in terms of chief factors is also established. This leads to the introduction of the $π$-Fitting ideal of a skew brace, for which we prove a local analogue of Fitting's theorem and provide a description in terms of centralisers of chief factors. Finally, we introduce the $π$-core of a skew brace and investigate its relationship with $π$-ideals and central $π$-nilpotency.

title: On δ-derivations of \mathfrak{saff}_{n+1}
abstract: We study $δ$-derivations of the finite-dimensional perfect Lie algebra $\mathfrak{saff}_{n+1}=\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})\ltimes\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$, where $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ is the natural $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$-module. For $n>1$ and $δ\ne1$, we prove that every nonzero $δ$-derivation occurs at $δ=\frac12$ and is a scalar multiple of the identity. For $n=1$, we explicitly describe the four-dimensional space of $(-2)$-derivations.

title: Factorizations by column blocks and Schubert polynomials as products of key polynomials
abstract: We classify the Schubert polynomials that are products of key polynomials and explicitly determine their finest key factorization. Their indexing permutations are precisely those avoiding ten classical patterns of length six, which form the minimal pattern basis. More generally, the connected components of the column interaction graph give the unique finest factorization of a dual flagged Weyl character into nonconstant diagram characters. Every other such factorization is obtained by grouping these components. We also prove Makhija's conjecture on products of elementary symmetric polynomials in initial alphabets, allowing repeated alphabets. In this case, the elementary factors are uniquely determined, up to order, by the nonempty Rothe columns.

title: Robust global supply chain reconfiguration under tariff and geopolitical uncertainty
abstract: Global supply chains are increasingly exposed to trade policy shocks and physical disruptions arising from common geopolitical events. We develop a robust optimization framework with two decision stages for strategic supply chain reconfiguration. Supplier qualification and transportation arc activation decisions are made before uncertainty is realized, while operational flows adapt afterward. Geopolitical uncertainty is represented through country level shocks that can jointly trigger tariff escalation, policy induced restrictions on cross border capacity, facility disruptions, and physical transportation failures. The resulting min max min problem is reformulated by dualizing the operational recourse problem, yielding a nonconvex mixed integer bilinear adversarial problem solved within a column and constraint generation procedure. Comparison with complete enumeration verifies the implementation on small instances, while experiments on 60 synthetic supply chain networks of varying sizes assess computational performance. The results show that omitting geopolitical transmission channels during strategic design can lead to substantial deterioration in cost and service under full geopolitical stress. Broader protection is achieved primarily through changes in transportation network configuration rather than increased supplier qualification. Robust performance also depends on the severity and composition of geopolitical consequences, with restrictions on cross border capacity exerting a stronger effect than comparable proportional changes in tariff severity over the tested ranges. A geographically grounded case analysis further shows that the value of individual uncertainty channels depends on network structure and geographic exposure.

title: Bethe Cycles, Frobenius Identities, and Quantum/Classical Duality
abstract: We study Frobenius action on the trigonometric Ruijsenaars--Schneider system associated with cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties. The construction continues the program initiated by Etingof and Varchenko and developed in quantum $K$-theory by the author and Smirnov. We explain how the monodromy eigenvectors recently constructed by Tarasov and Varchenko fit the quantum/classical duality between Bethe equations and tRS level sets. At a root of unity, all partial shifts cancel in the Newton--Adams combinations of the tRS Hamiltonians, leaving precisely the operators obtained by Frobenius action. This proves compatibility of the joint eigenvalue problem with Frobenius action in every rank and at every root order.

title: Compact generation and perfect objects in homotopy categories of exact model structures
abstract: Compact generation allows large triangulated categories to be studied through suitably small objects. For homotopy categories arising from exact model structures, a natural question is how this intrinsic notion of smallness relates to finite presentation in the underlying exact category. In this paper, we investigate this relation for hereditary projective model structures generated by finitely presented Gorenstein projective objects. We establish compact generation and study the stronger requirement that every compact object admits a finitely presented cofibrant representative. We call objects with such representatives perfect. Under local coherence and the existence of enough projectives among the finitely presented objects, the finitely presented cofibrant objects form a Frobenius category whose stable category describes the perfect objects and whose idempotent completion recovers all compact objects. The relative $Q$-shaped setting, for suitable small categories $Q$, makes explicit how these finiteness properties depend on the choice of exact structure. The pure exact structure yields a compactly generated homotopy category, called the $Q$-shaped pure derived category. On the other hand, the split exact structure yields the $Q$-shaped homotopy category, which is compactly generated only in the pure semisimple case, analogously to the classical homotopy category of complexes. Finally, for acyclic $Q$ and for left artinian rings, we show that every compact object admits a strictly perfect representative. In particular, we establish that compact and perfect objects coincide, proving the conjecture of Holm and Jorgensen under these hypotheses.

title: Multidimensional Infinite-Horizon Markovian Backward Stochastic Differential Equations with Continuous Coefficients and Nonzero-Sum Differential Games
abstract: This paper addresses the solvability of multidimensional infinite-horizon Markovian backward stochastic differential equations with continuous coefficients. We do not require the Lipschitz property or other quantitative controls of differences, and each component of the generator is allowed to depend simultaneously on all components of the multidimensional backward variables. A local L^q-domination framework adapted to the infinite-horizon setting is developed and combined with our linear flow conjugacy analysis to obtain the required distributional control in the presence of unbounded linear drift. We also derive a common Markov representation valid for the entire family of initial states. The analytical obstacles arising from weak regularity and the multidimensional structure are thereby overcome. Furthermore, we consider a class of infinite-horizon nonzero-sum differential games with a general non linear structure, allowing player controls to be fully coupled and permitting payoff criteria that are not restricted to an exponential discount form, establish an equivalence between the game and the corresponding multidimensional infinite-horizon backward stochastic differential equations, and prove the existence of a Nash equilibrium.

title: All Strict Calabi--Yau Threefolds of Height One Lift to Characteristic 0
abstract: We prove that every strict Calabi--Yau threefold of Artin--Mazur height one over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0 admits a projective lift to W(k). No assumption is made on the torsion in its crystalline cohomology, and p is arbitrary. Using the crystalline period map of Brantner and Taelman, we show that the obstruction to extending a lift over W_n(k) is the Bockstein of a torsion coordinate of its period point, and that this coordinate can always be made to vanish by varying the lift. The mixed-characteristic deformation functor need not be smooth: for a Calabi--Yau threefold of height one constructed by Addington and Bragg in characteristic 3, some lifts over W_2(k) do not extend over W_3(k). This disproves a conjecture of Achinger and Zdanowicz.

title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
abstract:
Let $\mathcal{B}_α$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_α^k$ on $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$
  if and only if $-1<α\leq1$. We also show that, for every $α>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.

title: Finite Tensor 2-Categories
abstract:
We propose a definition of a finite linear 2-category, as a 2-categorical analogue of the notion of a finite abelian category of Etingof-Ostrik. We go on to prove that finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives are precisely the Morita 2-categories of (all) algebras in a finite multitensor category. Thus, finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives can be viewed as `non-semisimple' generalizations of the finite semisimple 2-categories of Douglas-Reutter.
  Secondly, we study finite multitensor 2-categories, that is, finite linear 2-categories equipped with a monoidal structure for which every objects has duals. We extend several results about fusion 2-categories to our present setting. In particular, we investigate the properties of the 2-category of bimodules over a rigid algebra $\mathcal{A}$ in a finite tensor 2-category $\mathfrak{C}$. We show that, if $\mathfrak{C}$ has adjunctible projectives, then the 2-category of $\mathcal{A}$-$\mathcal{A}$-bimodules in $\mathfrak{C}$ is a finite multitensor 2-category. This construction provides many examples of finite tensor 2-categories. For instance, the Drinfeld center of a finite tensor 2-category with adjunctible projectives is a finite tensor 2-category.

title: Dependent choice and iterated beta_n-model reflection
abstract: In this paper, we consider conservation results for iterated $β_n$-model reflection principles. Using these principles, we characterize the $Π^1_{m+2}$-, $Σ^1_{m+2}$- and $\mathsf{B}(Π^1_{m+2})$-consequences of $Σ^1_{n+1}$-$\mathsf{DC}_0$ and $Σ^1_{n+1}$-$\mathsf{TDC}_0$ for $m \leq n$. Here, $\mathsf{B}(Π^1_{m+2})$ denotes the set of Boolean combinations of $Π^1_{m+2}$-formulas, and $\mathsf{TDC}$ stands for transfinite $\mathsf{DC}$. We also show that, in each case, the stronger theory has a super-exponential speed-up over the corresponding conservative subtheory.

title: Sharp global \(L^2\) estimates for oscillatory integral operators with quasi-homogeneous phases
abstract:
For one-dimensional oscillatory integral operators with real-analytic phases, the seminal work of Phong and Stein established that the Newton polygon of the mixed Hessian of the phase determines the sharp local \(L^2\)-decay. The local theory relies on spatial localization near the origin and therefore does not capture the global geometry of the real zero set of the Hessian. For globally defined operators, unbounded real zero curves of the Hessian can make the global decay strictly slower than the local decay or destroy \(L^2\)-boundedness altogether.
  We establish a global analogue of the Phong--Stein theory for quasi-homogeneous polynomial phases. We introduce a family of Newton polygons adapted to the regions near and away from the real zero curves of the Hessian, together with the corresponding box-area scales. The relative geometry of these Newton polygons and area scales characterizes global \(L^2\)-boundedness and determines the sharp \(L^2\)-estimates in the high- and low-frequency regimes. As an application, we determine the exact range of anisotropic homogeneous \(L^2\)-Sobolev estimates for the associated global Radon transform.

title: Factorization of Elliptic Divisibility Sequences via Modular Curves
abstract: In this paper, we give a structural factorization of elliptic divisibility sequences in terms of finitely many modular functions on the modular curve $X_1(N)$. More precisely, we express the functions obtained by pulling back division polynomials along the universal torsion section as products of fixed modular factors. Then we show that this factorization is compatible with the natural action of $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ on the modular curve $X_1(N)$ and so descends to the modular curve $X_0(N)$ via the norm map. As applications, we obtain a perfect power criterion, local and global growth estimates for the associated elliptic divisibility sequences.

title: Removing Trace Preservation from a Universal Spectral Bound for 2-Positive Maps
abstract: Vom Ende, Chruściński, Kimura and Muratore-Ginanneschi proved that every 2-positive trace-preserving map $Φ$ on $M_d=M_d(\mathbb{C})$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}Φ\le d\,m(Φ) + d^2 - d$, where $m(Φ)$ is the smallest real part of an eigenvalue of $Φ$, and deduced the universal relaxation-rate bound $\operatorname{Tr} L \le d\,m(L)$ for generators of 2-positive trace-preserving semigroups. They asked whether trace preservation is needed, and conjectured that every conditionally 2-positive map $L$, i.e. every $L$ for which $e^{tL}$ is 2-positive for all $t \ge 0$, satisfies $\operatorname{Tr} L \le d\,m(L) + (d^2 - d)\,s(L)$, where $s(L)$ is the largest real part of an eigenvalue of $L$. We prove this conjecture. The argument normalizes a 2-positive map by a positive definite eigenmatrix of its Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint, which turns it into a 2-positive trace-preserving map in the manner of a quantum Doob transform. The existence of such an eigenmatrix is guaranteed after adding an arbitrarily small multiple of the unnormalized depolarizing map, and the inequality then passes to the limit by continuity of the spectrum. No irreducibility, diagonalizability or faithful-invariant-state assumption is required. We also show that the constant $d$ is optimal within the class of non-trace-preserving completely positive semigroups, and we recast the result as a universal constraint on decay rates measured relative to the dominant spectral growth rate.

title: Near-quadratic sum-product estimates in fixed number fields
abstract: Let $K$ be a fixed number field. We prove a quantitative expansion theorem for mixed sumsets $A+B$, assuming only that $A$ is covered by relatively few cosets of a multiplicative group of small finite valuation rank. The constants are independent of the generators, their heights, and their prime ideal supports. As a consequence, if $A\subset K^\times$, $|A|=N\ge 3$, and each element has nonzero valuation at at most $k$ finite places, then every $B\subset K$ with $|B|=N$ satisfies $$ \max\{|A+B|,|AA|\} \ge N^2\exp\left[-C_K\left((k+1)\log(\log N+2)+\sqrt{(k+1)\log N}\right)\right]. $$ This is $N^{2-o(1)}$ for $k=o(\log N/\log\log N)$. We also obtain a trade-off between the additive and multiplicative deficits, estimates for iterated linear sumsets, and a transfer theorem for product constructions $A=PG$ in terms of the multiplicative deficit of $P$. The proof recovers local scales from an exact sum and bounds the remaining conditional entropy by the overlap of entropy measures on fixed trees.

title: A class of degenerate elliptic problems involving the Grushin operator: critical mass and ground states
abstract: We study the following degenerate elliptic equation with combined nonlinearities and prescribed mass \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \begin{cases} -Δ_γu+ωu+|u|^{p-2}u=|u|^{q-2}u \ \ \mbox{in }\mathbb{R}^{N}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N}} |u|^{2} \mathrm{d}z=c, \end{cases} \end{aligned} \end{equation*} where $Δ_γ$ is the Grushin operator and $ω\in\mathbb{R}$ appears as an unknown Lagrange multiplier. We characterize the critical mass threshold and the energy ground state solutions. Firstly, we prove the existence of optimizers for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality involving the Grushin operator together with estimates for the related best constant. Secondly, we characterize the critical mass by the best constant of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality and prove the existence of $x$-radial energy ground state solutions. Finally, we describe the relation between the $x$-radial action and energy ground state solutions, and the optimizers of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. The strategy developed here is based on the interplay between the mass-preserving scaling and a sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. It therefore suggests possible extensions to other prescribed-mass problems with competing homogeneous terms and threshold-mass phenomena.

title: Topology of rational equivalence closures and Lawson homology
abstract: Rational equivalence need not be closed in the Chow topology, and its closure can have infinitely generated homotopy groups. For a connected reduced complex projective variety, we prove that this closure is locally contractible and that its quotient in the algebraically trivial cycles is a finite or countable weak product of circles. The quotient map admits a global continuous section. Consequently, the higher homotopy of the cycle space is carried by the closure and is canonically identified with Lawson homology. We describe the remaining fundamental group quotient and its integral Walker comparison. Applications include smooth projective examples with infinite rank closure homotopy throughout prescribed finite intervals and a family of abelian threefolds with four simultaneously dense, nonconstructible quotient rank strata.

title: A characterization of equality in the edge-localized Bollobás-Nikiforov inequality
abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge2$. Let $e(G)$ and $ω(G)$ denote its number of edges and clique number, respectively. Let $λ_1(G)\ge\cdots\geλ_n(G)$ be its adjacency eigenvalues. In 2007, Bollobás and Nikiforov conjectured that every graph $G\neq K_n$ satisfies $λ_1^2(G)+λ_2^2(G)\le2\left(1-\frac1{ω(G)}\right)e(G).$ This conjecture was recently completely resolved by Coutinho, Liu, Spier, Tang and Zhang. For every edge $e\in E(G)$, let $c_G(e)$ denote the maximum order of a clique containing $e$. Kannan, Kumar and Pragada proposed the edge-localized conjecture $λ_1^2(G)+λ_2^2(G)\le2\sum_{e\in E(G)}\left(1-\frac1{c_G(e)}\right)$ for every graph $G\neq K_n$. This conjecture was subsequently proved by Shaik. In this paper, we provide complete structural characterizations of the equality cases in both the Bollobás-Nikiforov inequality and its edge-localized version.

title: Principal profiles, characteristic communication and critical asymptotics for cooperative nonlocal systems on the circle
abstract: We study cooperative nonlocal transport on a circle with species-dependent constant velocities and arbitrary $L^1$ probability kernels. For periodic coefficients, the period map is a compact perturbation of the no-jump map. We construct separate receiving and sending characteristic scans: under a two-tree condition based at one active component, a positive Floquet profile exists exactly when the full period map has strictly larger spectral radius than its no-jump part. The other jump rates may vanish. The scans provide an integral minorant and positive jump return; a separate coefficient inequality verifies the spectral gap. Smooth locking examples distinguish communication from frozen-time mixing, while a resonant example separates positive return from spectral separation. Autonomous nonzero velocities and union-graph connectivity yield a simple principal pair; one active component suffices for exponential mixing. We also prove local perturbation results. For quadratic self-regulation, the same principal projection gives a transverse response whose averaged cubic coefficient is a nonnegative asymptotic variance. It determines both the critical $t^{-2}\log t$ correction and the second-order period-averaged amplitude of the positive branch.

title: The numerical range of limits of real rational functions
abstract: Given two nonzero polynomials $f, g \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ vanishing at the origin $0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we study the numerical range of the limit $$ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}, $$ denoted by $\mathcal{R}_{f,g}$, which is defined as the set of all possible limits of the rational function $\displaystyle\frac{f}{g}$ as $x$ tends to $0$. When $n = 2$ and $g$ has a non-isolated zero at $0$, we describe all possible forms of $\mathcal{R}_{f,g}$ and provide an effective algorithm to compute this set based on Puiseux expansions. This is a follow-up to our recent results~\cite{Dinh2025}, in which we only considered the case when $0$ is an isolated zero of $g$.

title: Pointwise decay of cumulants and scaling regimes of chaotic states
abstract: We consider nonequilibrium chaotic states of classical interacting particles in a family of scaling limits motivated by kinetic theory. The particle activity and the strength of the pair interaction are rescaled simultaneously, allowing for both dilute and non-dilute regimes. Using cluster expansion, we derive pointwise bounds for truncated correlation functions (cumulants) of arbitrary order. We cover stable finite-range interactions and repulsive Riesz potentials, including non-integrable tails in bounded macroscopic domains.

title: Sensitivity of RMS Delay Spread Estimation to Power Delay Profile Thresholding in Time-Varying Channels at 33 GHz
abstract: Root mean square (RMS) delay spread is a key parameter characterizing temporal dispersion in radio propagation channels. Its estimation from measured power delay profiles (PDPs), however, depends strongly on the adopted power threshold. This paper investigates the sensitivity of RMS delay spread estimates to relative PDP thresholding in a time-varying millimeter-wave channel at 33 GHz. The analysis uses wideband channel sounding measurements conducted in a dynamic road environment with moving vehicles. The temporal evolution and empirical cumulative distributions of RMS delay spread are evaluated for thresholds ranging from -20 to -50 dB. Reducing the threshold increases the median RMS delay spread from approximately 140 to 168 ns and the 90th percentile from 200 to 210 ns. Both statistics converge at lower thresholds, with -40 dB providing a practical convergence level. The results emphasize the importance of threshold selection for reliable channel characterization and consistent comparison of measurements.

title: Characterization of Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
abstract:
The aim of this paper is to obtain the characterization of Fourier transform for functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $H$, defined on the groups $G=\R^n,\,G=\Z/n\Z$. In the first part of the paper, we consider the Fourier transform as a bijective mapping on $S_H$, the space of all $H$-valued smooth rapidly decaying functions on $\R^n$, which naturally extends bijectively to the dual space $S_H'$. Within this framework, we characterize the Fourier transform in terms of the convolution theorem, supplemented by additional structural properties of the Fourier transform. In the second part of the paper, we consider the discrete setting, where the Fourier transform is an operator on $L^1(\Z/n\Z, H)$, and we provide corresponding characterization based on its essential properties.
  In contrast to the classical setting, a key assumption in our framework involves the interplay between two distinct convolution operations. As a consequence, the structure of our proof diverges notably from the classical case and introduces additional complexities.

title: Emergence of large densities in a chemotaxis system with signal-dependent motility
The Kothe Radical in Novikov Algebras
abstract: We study the Kothe radical (the upper nil radical) in the variety of Novikov algebras. We prove that the class of weakly right nilpotent Novikov algebras coincides with the class of r-nil algebras and forms a radical class. We establish that the Kothe radical is a hereditary radical in the variety of Novikov algebras. Furthermore, we obtain a structural description of the Kothe radical as the intersection of ideals whose corresponding quotient algebras are prime K-semisimple algebras. Finally, we construct an example of a prime r-nil Novikov algebra over a field of characteristic p>0, which implies that the Baer radical is strictly contained in the Kothe radical in this case.

title: The unilateral 2-linkage problem
abstract:
We study a new variant of the classical linkage problem for digraphs, which we call {\bf unilateral linkages.} A digraph $D$ is {\bf unilaterally $\bm{k}$-linked} if it satisfies that for every choice of $2k$ distinct vertices $s_1,s_2,\ldots{},s_k,t_1,t_2,\ldots{},t_k$ there are vertex disjoint directed paths $P_1,\ldots{},P_k$ in $D$ such that $P_i$ is either an $(s_i,t_i)$-path or a $(t_i,s_i)$-path for each $i\in [k]$. This is a relaxation of the property of $D$ being $k$-linked, where we insist that each $P_i$ must go from $s_i$ to $t_i$. Clearly every $k$-linked digraph is also unilaterally $k$-linked.
  It is easy to see that the unilateral linkage problem is NP-complete for general digraphs and that it is trivial for semicomplete digraphs (digraphs with no pair of non-adjacent vertices). We show how Thomassen's construction of highly connected digraphs which are not 2-linked can be modified to show that there is no connectivity which guarantees that a digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. We show that every 4-strong split digraph and every 5-strong semicomplete multipartite digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. Both bounds are best possible. A digraph is {\bf co-bipartite} if its vertex set can be covered by two induced semicomplete digraphs. We prove that every 6-strong co-bipartite digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. Here we do not know whether the correct answer is 5. We also prove that every 16-strong digraph with independence number at most 2 is unilaterally 2-linked.

title: Maximum Energy of Integral Circulant Graphs with Same-Parity Exponents
abstract: The energy of a finite graph is the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Let n be p to the power a times q to the power b, where p and q are distinct primes at least five and a and b, both positive integers, have the same parity. Among all nonempty sets D of proper divisors of n, the energy of the corresponding integral circulant graph is maximised by exactly two divisor sets: the divisors p to the power i times q to the power j with i plus j odd, and the divisors with i plus j even after removing p to the power a times q to the power b. We also determine the exact maximum energy. For the proof, weighted prime-power Ramanujan transforms yield an exact tensor-product representation of the graph energy, reducing the extremal problem to a weighted cut separating two prescribed vertices. After a sign conjugation, the relevant transforms decompose into embedded path blocks; the nontrivial blocks correspond to a weighted path together with chords of length three of weight negative one. We prove a sharp lower bound for cuts separating the two prescribed vertices in Kronecker products of these path blocks. For products of two such nontrivial blocks, equality holds only for cuts that isolate one of the two prescribed vertices. Combined with the energy-to-cut correspondence, these equality cases yield exactly the two maximising divisor sets.

title: An inverse moving point source problem in inhomogeneous acoustic media: uniqueness, stability and reconstruction
abstract: This paper is concerned with the simultaneous recovery of the trajectory and intensity of an unknown moving point source in an inhomogeneous acoustic medium. We prove that the whole-boundary measurements over a finite time interval uniquely determine the moving source. Furthermore, under suitable propagation and rank assumptions, Lipschitz stability of determining both the trajectory and intensity is derived using waveforms measured at four fixed receivers outside the source region. A novel Volterra--Euler reconstruction scheme is developed for solving the inverse problem, and the error estimate is derived for the proposed scheme. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed numerical method.

title: Bridgeland stability and Gieseker stability I: Limit stability
abstract:
We study the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability conditions on smooth projective varieties. For each fixed ray in a suitable angular sector, we prove that an object of $\mathrm{D}^b(X)$ is Bridgeland (semi)stable in the corresponding hearts for all sufficiently large radii if and only if it is a pure $H$-Gieseker (semi)stable sheaf. In this sector, we identify the category of coherent sheaves as the limiting heart in the sense of eventual membership. We also identify a perverse coherent limiting heart in the opposite angular sector.
  The key ingredients are uniform HN-phase estimates for bounded families of pure sheaves, coefficient bounds for the coherent images of potential destabilizers, and a criterion forcing narrow exact sequences in the varying hearts to be bounded saturated coherent sequences.

title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
abstract: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503--1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522--1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].

title: Finite Matrix Rings of Even Size Are Determined by Their Commuting Graphs
abstract: The commuting graph of a noncommutative ring has its noncentral elements as vertices, with two distinct vertices adjacent when they commute. Akbari, Ghandehari, Hadian and Mohammadian conjectured that a full matrix ring over a finite field is determined, among rings with identity, by its commuting graph. In this paper, we prove the conjecture for every even matrix size.

title: ROAR: Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate Heuristic for Large and Extreme Scale Traveling Repairman Problem
abstract: The Traveling Repairman Problem minimizes cumulative arrival times rather than the total route length, as in the classical Traveling Salesman Problem. The literature contains several legacy metaheuristics for the TRP; however, most are evaluated on small- and medium-scale instances and show limited scalability for large and extreme datasets. GILS-RVND, the current gold standard in metaheuristic algorithms, performs well on small and medium instances but struggles to scale due to the exhaustive neighborhood search in the RVND phase. To address this limitation, we introduce Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate (ROAR), a Large Neighborhood Search-based method that integrates ruin-and-recreate with greedy insertion and a restricted, insertion-anchored 2-opt operator. Computational experiments demonstrate that ROAR produces high-quality solutions for large-scale instances and outperforms existing methods under strict time limits. We further introduce an O(1)-time, O(1)-space algorithm for evaluating 2-opt moves during a contiguous systematic sweep, which, to the best of our knowledge, is unprecedented. Finally, we evaluate ROAR on instances with up to 200,000 nodes, substantially exceeding the largest instances previously reported in the literature (11,849 nodes).

title: Spectral delocalization and central limit theorems for Fourier functionals of stationary Gaussian fields
abstract:
We characterize Gaussian fluctuations of Fourier-Hermite functionals of stationary Gaussian fields on locally compact Abelian groups via spectral delocalization: conditional on the total spectral sum being near the probed frequency, no partial sum concentrates. Under suitable assumptions, this reduces Gaussian convergence to small-ball estimates for convolution powers of the spectral measure, without model-specific contraction estimates.
  On $\mathbb T^d$, the criterion yields CLTs at every fixed frequency for band-limited fields and random trigonometric polynomials, and extends the known failure of Gaussian convergence for planar arithmetic random waves from the fourth chaos to all even orders $q\ge4$. On $\mathbb R^d$ and $\mathbb Z^d$, we establish a Breuer-Major theorem for Fourier functionals at every frequency with nonzero limiting variance. Cyclical long-memory models exhibit frequency-dependent Gaussian convergence.
  We also establish CLTs and variance asymptotics for singular continuous spectral measures, including those of stationary Gaussian solutions of linear PDEs. At zero frequency, weak Ahlfors regularity of the spectral support and an $L^2$ density suffice for second-chaos CLTs, covering fractal sets, the Airy surface of Gaussian sea waves, and smooth compact manifolds. For a class of smooth hypersurfaces, we obtain the same variance rates and CLTs known for classical nonlinear functionals of Berry's random wave model. Finally, for random waves with spherical spectral densities bounded above and below, we classify Gaussian convergence at every frequency $\|z\|\le q$: it fails only for the planar second chaos when $0<\|z\|<2$.

title: Observer-Based Event-Triggered Control of Infinite-Dimensional Linear Systems
abstract:
We investigate observer-based event-triggered stabilization of infinite-dimensional linear systems, such as those governed by partial differential equations. A Luenberger observer and a feedback gain are assumed to stabilize the closed loop in continuous time, and we study what happens when the control input is only updated at instants generated by a dynamic event-triggering mechanism. Unlike approaches that rely on state-dependent triggering rules, our condition only involves the observer state and the measured output, which makes it implementable when the full state is not measured. It compares the deviation of a monitored signal of the observer since the last update with a threshold made of two parts. The first one is a relative part, proportional to the current size of this signal, and the second one is a positive internal variable, which does not depend on the observer state. In particular, the case where the threshold reduces to the internal variable alone is covered.
  Under suitable assumptions, we establish the well-posedness of the closed-loop system and the absence of Zeno behavior for general choices of these two parts, and we prove its exponential stability under a small-gain condition on the relative part. We further analyse the existence of a dwell-time, namely a positive lower bound on the time elapsed between two consecutive triggering instants. When the sampled dynamics is bounded, as in finite-dimensional systems or systems with a finite-dimensional unstable part, we obtain a dwell-time independent of the initial data, together with exponential stability. For unbounded generators, we exhibit a system satisfying all our assumptions for which no triggering rule can achieve both a dwell-time independent of the initial data and bounded trajectories.

title: A nilpotent version of the first Kac conjecture
abstract: We derive a formula for the nilpotent Kac polynomial and define an explicit generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra (by generators and relations) and conjecture that its graded dimensions recover the constant terms of the nilpotent Kac polynomial. We outline empirical evidence supporting the conjecture and prove it for two special classes of quivers: quivers without oriented cycles except loops and quivers with "negative enough" Euler form.

title: On Some Lie Group Invariant noncommutative functions
abstract: We study noncommutative polynomials and functions invariant under linear actions of infinite (compact Lie) groups, with a focus on $SU(2)$ acting on two noncommuting variables. For $SU(2)$, we give a complete description of the invariant noncommutative polynomials: there are no invariants of odd degree, and in degree $2n$ the invariants are exactly the span of the $S_{2n}$-orbit of $(XY-YX)^n$. We also construct an explicit basis recursively from the operation $(A,B)\mapsto XAYB-YAXB$, and show that the space of degree-$2n$ invariants has dimension equal to the $n$-th Catalan number. All proofs proceed by direct computation with the Haar integral.

title: Representations of shifted quantum affine algebras and cluster algebras II: Non simply-laced types and cluster expansions
abstract: We extend our previous results on cluster structures in the Grothendieck rings of categories $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for shifted quantum affine algebras to the non-simply laced types. We also show that, for all types, the formal power series expressions of the cluster monomials in terms of classes of positive prefundamental representations can be regarded as limits of cluster expansions, thus establishing their positivity.

title: A minimising principle for interval covers of zigzag persistence modules
abstract: Zigzag persistence modules serve as an essential tool in topological data analysis. The fundamental theorem of persistent homology states that any zigzag persistence module decomposes into a direct sum of simple building blocks called interval modules. We consider an interval cover, a possibly redundant family of interval submodules spanning every vertex space of a finite zigzag persistence module. We give an elementary descent argument that replaces a redundant cover with a minimal one that is an interval decomposition. This provides an optimisation perspective on persistence modules and their interval decomposition. As an application, we give an estimate of the generalised rank invariant in terms of a cover.

title: Quantitative periodic homogenization and uniform regularity for nonlocal equations
abstract: In this work, we study quantitative homogenization for a class of nonlocal equations with periodically oscillating Hölder continuous coefficients. For Dirichlet problems in bounded $C^{1,α}$ domains, we prove $L^2$ convergence rates that are expected to be optimal. In addition, we establish interior Lipschitz estimates and optimal boundary Hölder estimates for weak solutions, with constants independent of the period of oscillation.

title: Approximate Counting for Mixed $p$-Spin Glasses in Weak External Fields via Cluster Expansion
abstract: We give algorithms for approximating the partition function $Z_N$ of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) model and finite mixed Ising $p$-spin models with $p\ge 3$. The algorithms apply at a fixed margin below the second-moment threshold $β_{\mathrm f}$ with homogeneous weak external fields $|h|\leqρ_0N^{-1/4}$, for fixed $ρ_0>0$. For any accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and failure parameter $δ\in(0,1)$, they approximate $\log Z_N$ to additive error $\varepsilon$. The number of exact operations is polynomial jointly in $N$, $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $δ^{-1}$. The disorder variables have i.i.d symmetric distribution with unit variance. The failure probability is at most $δ$ plus an explicit disorder tail bound. This tail bound tends to zero under a finite fourth moment condition. Our approach builds on the cluster expansions of Aizenman--Lebowitz--Ruelle~\cite{ALR87} and Dey--Wu~\cites{DW23,DW26}. For higher-order mixtures, we retain hypergraphs using few vertices and evaluate their total weight deterministically through local spin averages and inclusion--exclusion. For SK, we impose cutoffs on the number of vertices of degree at least three and on the total number of edges. We estimate the retained sum using randomized color coding~\cite{AYZ95}. A lower tail control based on reverse hypercontractivity~\cite{MOS13} converts the mean-square approximation of the normalized partition function into logarithmic accuracy.

title: On $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles on $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are small modifications of a Fano fourfold
abstract: We find necessary conditions for the projectivization of a rank two vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{C}}$ to be related to a smooth Fano 4-fold by a small $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial modification (SQM). Furthermore, we fully describe the birational geometry of $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$ when $\mathcal{E}$ is stable, with $c_1=-1$, $c_2=2$. In this case, we prove that there exists a flip from $X^+$ to $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$, where $X^+$ is smooth and Fano. We also determine the birational geometry and numerical invariants of $X^+$.

title: Finite-Resolution Physics from Additivity Symmetry
abstract:
Quantum field theory unifies special relativity and quantum mechanics, yet relies on externally imposed prescriptions for quantization, renormalization, and probabilistic interpretation that lack a common algebraic foundation. This work derives these features from a single principle: the finite-resolution realization of the additive group (R, +) under four consistency constraints: finite operational resolution (FR1), multiplicative linearity (FR2), phase coherence (FR3), and statistical typicality (FR4).
  The Hilbert-space formalism of quantum theory, the Born probability rule, and the Kolmogorov structure of statistical mechanics emerge as limiting projections of a common additive algebra, without additional postulates. Extending this framework to spacetime translations and their automorphisms, we recover the kinematic and dynamical structure of quantum field theory and address ultraviolet divergences through intrinsic finiteness rather than external renormalization.
  Quantization and unitarity emerge from additive symmetry, while the gravitational field is interpreted as the algebraic kernel transporting boundary information into bulk observables, without requiring an independent quantization of the metric. This framework aims to provide a unified, finite, and algebraic foundation for physical law.nite, and algebraic foundation for physical law.

title: The packing and covering number of trees are local
abstract: For a graph, its $r$-packing number is the size of the largest $r$-separated set and its $r$-covering number is the size of the smallest $r$-net. We show that the $r$-covering number and $r$-packing number are continuous in the fringe topology on locally finite trees. This recovers convergence results by Meir and Moon for e.g. uniform binary trees, uniform plane trees, uniform Polyá trees and random recursive trees, and proves new results for many other tree models, such as size-conditioned Bienaymé trees, simply generated trees, $m$-ary search trees, the minimum spanning tree of the complete graph and preferential attachment trees. Moreover, our formulation provides an intuitive interpretation of the limiting constant, that also provides an easy route for explicit computations in the case of size-conditioned Bienaymé trees. Our method relies on the definition of a canonical minimum $r$-net, and a relation between covering numbers and packing numbers due to Meir and Moon.

title: Constructing Data-Driven Budgeted Uncertainty Sets for Robust Optimization
abstract: In robust optimization, budgeted uncertainty sets offer a popular trade-off between modeling flexibility and computational tractability. Data that is observed in practice is often discrete in nature, which creates the need for tools to construct budgeted uncertainty sets based on observed data. This paper presents a principled approach for this purpose, which ensures that any solution found through the robust problem with respect to the constructed budgeted uncertainty set offers an approximation guarantee with respect to the optimal value of the problem with discrete data. Our approach is purely based on the geometry of data and can be applied to any nominal optimization problem. We discuss the problem of evaluating budgeted uncertainty sets, and how to construct them using exact and heuristic methods. In computational experiments, we show that it is possible to construct sets with little computation time that offer guarantees that are close to optimality.

title: Coprime matchings of divisor sets
abstract: For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ be its set of positive divisors and put $N:=τ(n)=|D(n)|$. We characterize the arithmetic progressions $\mathcal P$ of length $N$ that admit a bijection with $D(n)$ pairing relatively prime integers. Such a coprime matching exists if and only if, for every prime $p\mid n$, at most $N/(ν_p(n)+1)$ terms of $\mathcal P$ are divisible by $p$, where $ν_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$. Call $n$ an $M$-number if $p^p\nmid n$ for every prime $p$. We prove that $D(n)$ can be matched with every primitive arithmetic progression of length $N$, meaning one whose first term and common difference are coprime, if and only if $n$ is an $M$-number. This proves a conjecture of McNew and Pomerance. We call $n$ \emph{matchable} if $D(n)$ admits a coprime matching with the primitive arithmetic progression $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$. The general criterion implies that $n$ is matchable if and only if $\lfloor N/p\rfloor\le N/(ν_p(n)+1)$ for all $p\mid n$. We explicitly classify the matchable non-$M$-numbers, settle a conjectured divisor criterion, and prove that every divisor of a matchable integer is matchable. A Vandermonde determinant gives the required matchings under bounds on the prime exponents, while a partition into shorter progressions handles the remaining cases.

title: Global minimax rates for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation
abstract: Recent work established minimax rates for pointwise estimation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE), but the fundamental limits under global losses remained unresolved. We derive matching minimax lower and upper bounds under the $L_2$ and $L_\infty$ risks on certain covariate-density and support classes. For the lower bounds, we develop a many-fuzzy-hypotheses method that replaces each fixed alternative in a multiple-hypothesis construction with a mixture over nuisance functions that leaves its CATE unchanged. A localized product-mixture $χ^2$ bound is used to control the divergence of each resulting mixture from a common baseline, enabling multiple well-separated CATE hypotheses to be handled simultaneously. For the upper bounds, we analyze a modified local polynomial R-learner. The $L_2$ argument extends the pointwise bias--variance analysis, while the $L_\infty$ argument combines concentration inequalities for U-statistics with a continuity argument enabled by the use of a continuous kernel and additional regularity of the second-order basis. The resulting rates show that the pointwise elbow phenomenon persists globally: the $L_2$ transition threshold is unchanged, while the $L_\infty$ rate has an additional logarithmic factor and a transition threshold adjusted by $1-\log\log n/\log n$.

title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
abstract: We establish a quantitative local law for random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three. Away from the singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum, we obtain high-probability entrywise Green's function estimates down to spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$, uniformly in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps. As a consequence, we establish complete eigenvector delocalization: every normalized eigenvector $u$ whose eigenvalue stays a small but fixed positive distance away from the singular energies satisfies $\|u\|_\infty\leq(\log N)^C/\sqrt{N}$ with high probability.

title: Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
abstract: We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (Σ,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^α(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_Σ (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{α+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $α\to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^α$.

title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
abstract: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.

title: A Posteriori Error Analysis of Finite Element Approximation to an Evolution Equation with a Positive-Type Memory Term
abstract: This paper develops reliable a posteriori error estimates for finite element approximation of an evolution equation with a positive-type memory kernels on bounded convex polygonal or polyhedral domains, including both smooth and weakly singular kernels. For the weakly singular kernel $t^{α-1}/Γ(α),\; 0<α<1,$ the model captures the transition from parabolic diffusion to wave propagation, recovering the corresponding limiting equations as $α\to0^+$ and $α\to1^-$, respectively, with the memory term governing the intermediate dynamics. The spatial discretization employs time-dependent finite element spaces, while the backward Euler method combined with numerical quadrature is used for time integration. A unified \emph{a posteriori} analysis is established for both semidiscrete and fully discrete approximations. Elliptic reconstruction yields optimal spatial error estimates, while a memory-lag estimate preserves the essential cancellation in the convolution term, yielding a first-order temporal estimator whose kernel dependence is characterized by its integral. The resulting estimators are robust, with constants independent of the final time, spatial mesh size, and time step. Their kernel dependence involves only computable quantities, avoiding exponential growth in time. Moreover, for the weakly singular kernel, the $α$-dependent factors remain uniformly bounded for $α\in(0,1).$ Numerical experiments on a convex domain validate the theoretical results, and a space-time adaptive algorithm is also demonstrated on an L-shaped domain featuring a corner singularity and two temporal layers.

title: Mathematical Reality Capture: from the age of discoveries to mathematical topography and surveys
abstract: A proof answers a precise question, but mathematical understanding also grows through the relationships that its answer makes visible. A point measurement likewise differs from a photograph or a three-dimensional reconstruction of a building. In this work, we argue that, with the help of AI, mathematics should move from a discipline focused on isolated investigations of mathematical objects towards one capable of mapping them systematically. We therefore introduce the idea of "Mathematical Reality Capture", inspired by digital surveying and the reconstruction of a scene from several viewpoints. An elementary example shows how comparing algebra and geometry can illuminate the same phenomenon, provided that we distinguish diversity of explanations from validity of proof. From this analogy we derive criteria for building verifiable atlases, an experiment with which to assess their usefulness, and a reflection on the role of mathematicians in interpreting them.

title: Truncated $\mathcal{H}_2$ Optimal Model Order Reduction for Bilinear Quadratic Output Systems
abstract: We develop an $\mathcal{H}_2$ model reduction framework for polynomial bilinear systems with quadratic outputs. We define the associated $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm and show its consistency with the established norm in the original (non-polynomial) BQO case. We derive first-order necessary conditions for $\mathcal{H}_2$ optimal model reduction of these polynomial systems and use them to construct an efficient iterative algorithm for computing reduced BQO models that approximately satisfy these conditions. Numerical results on two examples demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed reduction approach.

title: Class numbers and finiteness of norm Euclidean quadratic lattices over algebraic number fields
abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraic number field and $\mathcal{O}_{F}$ the ring of integers of $F$. Let $L$ be an integral $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattice of rank $n\ge1$ on an anisotropic quadratic space $V$. We prove that if $L$ is norm Euclidean, then $L$ is $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-maximal of class number one, and the class number of $F$ equals the class number of $L\perp\mathbf{H}$, where $\mathbf{H}$ is the hyperbolic lattice with quadratic form $xy$. Under the same assumption, $F$ has class number one if $n\ge3$ and at most two if $n=1,2$. We also prove finiteness up to isometry for totally definite norm Euclidean lattices over totally real number fields in ranks at least three as the field varies, in rank two for fixed field degree, and in rank one over a fixed field. This confirms Clark's finiteness conjecture in ranks at least three.

title: Algebraic Completeness of Feynman Premeasures: The Henstock-Kurzweil Path Integral and Operator Wick Calculus in Lean 4
abstract: We formalize in Lean 4 the gauge closure of the Feynman functional integral for the free field without Wick rotation. First, the restriction to box divisions is removed via a direction bound and a uniform Riemann-sum estimate for all $δ$-fine cylindrical divisions. Second, the coordinate measure on $\mathbb{R}^k$ is identified with the standard Gaussian one. Third, the Saks-Henstock lemma and additivity are proved. Fourth, the Fresnel formula $\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{i a x^2/2} dx = \sqrt{2π/a} e^{iπ/4}$ is proved as an improper (gauge) integral. This yields the projective consistency of the oscillating Gaussian premeasure and the existence of the free-field integral. The free field is completely closed: we prove the Fresnel formula for an arbitrary symmetric positive-definite action $A$, compute the generating functional and the two-point function $\langle y_p y_q \rangle = i(A^{-1})_{pq}$, and prove Wick's theorem. The interacting field $λ\varphi^4$, unbounded generators, and renormalisation remain open. All results are machine-verified with no sorry or new axioms.

title: Optimal Control of Scalar Diffusions with Finite Action Sets
abstract: We study a scalar finite-horizon controlled diffusion with a finite action set. An action may affect the drift, the instantaneous variance, or both, and performance is assessed by a uniformly convex terminal deviation cost. The model represents systems in which decisions are made continuously in time but only finitely many operating settings are available. Under uniform nondegeneracy and an explicit shape condition on the terminal cost, we show that the value function is classical at positive times, establish global positive upper and lower bounds for its second state derivative, and prove that the ratio of its first and second state derivatives is strictly increasing. This ordering implies that each action's optimality region is connected, the active actions occur in monotone order, and adjacent regions are separated by unique switching boundaries. It also yields an exact coefficient-based screen that removes actions that cannot be optimal on any open state region. For smooth continuous-action benchmarks, both the value loss from restricting the action set and the additional loss from rounding the continuous optimal feedback to the nearest available action decrease quadratically with the action-set resolution. Numerical experiments illustrate the resulting action screens, threshold policies, and implementation losses.

title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
abstract: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.

title: Measuring Sudoku Difficulty: Formulation, Propagation and Uniqueness Certification
abstract: Finding a Sudoku completion and proving that the completion is unique are different computational tasks. Despite both concerning the same puzzle, their computational effort need not be closely related. In this paper, we investigate how this relationship depends on the mathematical formulation, solver and measure of computational effort. Using 32,000 uniquely solvable puzzles and 64 harder instances, we compare integer programming formulations and CP-SAT. Further, we prove that the raw natural formulation has an extremely weak linear programming relaxation, even with uniqueness exclusions. Computational experiments show that the relationship between completion and certification effort depends on the formulation, puzzle population, solver and effort measure, rather than on the puzzle alone.

title: A semigroup approach for rough partial differential equations with jumps
abstract: We establish an infinite-dimensional sewing lemma for discontinuous paths on a scale of Banach spaces. This allows us to construct Young and rough convolutions with jumps. Based on this we analyze the local and global well-posedness of semilinear parabolic rough partial differential equations (PDEs) with jumps in mixed space-time regularity spaces.
